dz.headline: Algerian president pardons 5,539 prisoners
dz.dek: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune granted presidential pardon to 5,539 inmates on the 72nd anniversary of the Revolution.
paragraphs: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has granted a presidential pardon to 5,539 inmates on the occasion of the 72nd anniversary of the Revolution of November 1, 1954. The Presidency of the Republic announced the decision on Saturday, October 31. This pardon applies to individuals, whether incarcerated or not, who received a final conviction before the decree was signed, provided their sentence or remaining sentence is 24 months or less.

However, the pardon does not extend to those convicted by military courts or for specific crimes including terrorism, treason, espionage, murder, drug trafficking, escape, parricide, violence against ascendants, indecent assault, and rape. Individuals convicted under law n° 06-01 related to corruption, money laundering, currency counterfeiting, smuggling, and infractions concerning foreign exchange and capital movements are also excluded.

The 72nd anniversary of the Revolution, celebrated on November 1, is a paid public holiday in Algeria. The additional evidence packet mentioned a weather alert for Algeria, with up to 40 mm of rain expected on Saturday and Sunday.

dz.headline: Algeria in talks to supply fertilizer to Bangladesh
dz.dek: Bangladesh, which imports 80% of its fertilizer, is seeking supply agreements with Algeria.
paragraphs: Bangladesh is seeking fertilizer supplies from Algeria as it imports 80% of its total demand. Discussions between the two nations advanced in September and October 2026, presenting a commercial opportunity for Algerian producers. No contract volumes or delivery schedules have been finalized yet.

The Bangladeshi Ministry of Agriculture confirmed the country's reliance on imports for its fertilizer needs. The Bangladeshi State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Humayun Kabir, urged stronger cooperation in fertilizers and energy with the Algerian ambassador in Dhaka on September 20. On October 5, Interior Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated Dhaka's intention to secure long-term fertilizer and LNG supply agreements.

The Bangladeshi newspaper The New Nation highlighted the potential partnership, calling for balanced supply agreements that consider product quality, prices, transport costs, financing, and delivery times. This move aims to boost economic cooperation between the two countries.

dz.headline: Russia vetoes US resolution on Western Sahara autonomy plan
dz.dek: Morocco's plan for Western Sahara autonomy faced international setback after Russia's veto of a US resolution.
paragraphs: Russia vetoed a United States resolution aimed at imposing Morocco's autonomy plan for Western Sahara on October 30. This action represents a significant disappointment for Morocco, which had previously normalized relations with Israel in September. Algerian diplomacy has consistently stated that sovereignty over a territory cannot be granted by a third party, regardless of global power.

Morocco had gambled on this plan in 2020, accepting a deal proposed by Donald Trump as part of the Abraham Accords. King Mohammed VI took a considerable risk, given domestic public support for Palestinians, especially after the Gaza war began. Morocco also invested heavily in arms deals and other agreements with Israel, even reportedly expelling Moroccans from their land for Israeli returnees.

The Moroccan government had interpreted Russia's abstention on resolution 2797 in October 2025 as a definitive closure of the Western Sahara issue in its favor. However, the text of the resolution did not eliminate the possibility of self-determination through a referendum, which is why Russia, China, and Algeria, then a non-permanent Security Council member, did not oppose it.

ao.headline: Angolan groups demand electoral transparency probe
ao.dek: Three civil society groups asked prosecutors to investigate the Ministry of Territorial Administration's handling of voter registration data.
paragraphs: Angolan civil society groups HANDEKA, UYELE, and MOSAICO have formally requested the Public Prosecutor's Office to launch a judicial inquiry into the Ministry of Territorial Administration (MAT). The organizations seek audits and accountability regarding the ministry's actions, particularly concerning the unofficial electoral registration process for next year's general elections.

The groups stated they have sought clarification from the MAT since June but received no response for over four months. They argue this institutional silence raises serious concerns about the ministry's legal duty to respond, the transparency of electoral administration, and citizens' right to scrutinize public administration acts. They specifically requested an investigation into the alleged failure to remove deceased individuals' records from the database of adult citizens.

The civil society organizations also called for an independent audit of the database and its computer file to assess integrity and legal compliance. They further demanded a financial audit of accounts and expenses related to the MAT's 'proof of life' operation. The groups emphasized that electoral registration transparency is a requirement of a democratic state, not a political concession, and reaffirmed their commitment to legality and citizens' political rights.

ao.headline: Angola struggles to admit foreign workers for factories
ao.dek: Government invites investment but immigration hurdles delay project starts and increase costs.
paragraphs: Angola's government actively seeks foreign investment to build factories and diversify its oil-dependent economy. However, foreign companies face significant obstacles when trying to secure visas and work permits for essential technical staff. Some investors have already spent large sums on construction but cannot bring in the necessary specialists, potentially halting equipment installation and production trials.

This issue goes beyond simple visa delays, indicating a structural problem in coordinating government departments responsible for investment, immigration, and labor. Investors consider the ease of bringing in skilled professionals a key factor when deciding where to commit capital. Without clear, stable, and legal pathways for these workers, investment pledges risk remaining unfulfilled.

The process of bringing industrial projects online, especially in heavy industry, can take years and relies heavily on specialized engineers. Delays in obtaining work permits for these professionals can lead to idle equipment, construction setbacks, and increased financial burdens for companies. These permits are integral to the successful construction and operation of industrial projects.

ao.headline: Africa's general governance improves unevenly
ao.dek: Infrastructure, health, and education show gains, but security and rule of law decline.
paragraphs: Africa's general governance saw improvements between 2016 and 2025, despite global shocks, according to the IIAG 2026 report. Progress was uneven, driven by economic and human development gains in 44 countries, covering 68% of the continent's population. Infrastructure, in particular, advanced across 52 countries, representing 84% of the population, with mobile connectivity, energy, and internet access improving.

Education advanced in 34 countries (75% of the population) and health in 40 countries (87% of the population). However, security, rule of law, and participation declined in 34 and 31 countries respectively, affecting 78% and 60% of Africans. Despite this, security deterioration slowed from 2022, with 27 countries showing improvements.

The report also noted that 25 countries, home to nearly 47% of the population, achieved economic progress even as security worsened. Economic opportunities advanced more in countries with better security, seen in 20 nations representing 22% of the population.

bj.headline: Benin bishops announce African traditional religion conference
bj.dek: The conference, scheduled for November 19-20, 2026, aims to foster mutual understanding between faiths.
paragraphs: The Episcopal Conference of Benin (CEB) will host an international conference on traditional African religion in Cotonou on November 19 and 20, 2026. The event will take place at the Saint-Charbel hall in Akpakpa.

This announcement was made in the final communique from the CEB's 79th ordinary plenary session, held in Natitingou from October 25 to 28. Organizers stated the goal is to deepen mutual knowledge between confessions and promote interreligious dialogue, linking it to African cultures and the continent's integral development.

The conference commemorates two past events involving Pope John Paul II: his 1986 meeting on peace in Assisi, Italy, and his 1993 visit to Cotonou where he met with leaders of indigenous religions and Vodun cults.

bj.headline: British PM open to slavery apology, rejects financial reparations
bj.dek: Andy Burnham proposes debt relief for poor nations instead of direct payments for historical slave trade role.
paragraphs: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has stated he is open to discussing official apologies for the UK's role in the transatlantic slave trade. In a statement published on October 30, Burnham proposed dialogue with affected countries and populations but rejected financial reparations.

Burnham clarified that this openness does not constitute an apology from the British state, suggesting it should be part of future discussions. He argued that current Britons cannot be held financially responsible for historical crimes they did not participate in. Instead, he proposed an international initiative to ease the debt burden of poor nations by extending repayment terms and lowering interest rates, with former Prime Minister Gordon Brown assisting.

Caribbean nations, including Jamaica, have presented a 10-point plan through CARICOM that includes apologies, support for health and education, and measures addressing the economic and social consequences of slavery. Jamaica submitted a petition to King Charles III on September 7, seeking referral of legal questions to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council regarding potential UK reparation obligations. These discussions are set to precede the Commonwealth leaders' summit on November 1 in Antigua and Barbuda.

bj.headline: Benin calls up Parfait Faton for CAN 2027 qualifiers
bj.dek: The Guépards will face the Central African Republic on November 12 and November 16 in Abidjan and Douala.
paragraphs: Benin's national football team, the Guépards, will play the Central African Republic on November 12 in Abidjan and November 16 in Douala for the third and fourth rounds of the CAN 2027 qualifiers. Midfielder Parfait Faton received his first call-up to the senior team, named among 25 players by coach Gernot Rohr on Saturday, October 31, 2026.

The squad includes experienced players like goalkeepers Marcel Dandjinou and Saturnin Allagbé, midfielders Sessi d’Almeida and Junior Olaïtan, and forwards Jodel Dossou, Aiyegun Tosin, Rodolfo Aloko, and Yamirou Ouorou. Dodo Dokou is also included in the group.
Benin currently has four points from their first two matches in Group F, having drawn 1-1 with Burkina Faso on September 25 and beaten Mauritania 2-1 on September 29 in Abidjan.

bw.headline: Journalist wins diamond at Botswana independence event
bw.dek: Veteran correspondent Joy Chikura received a diamond from Debswana at a national business conference dinner.
paragraphs: Duma FM news correspondent Joy Chikura won a diamond in a lucky draw at the Debswana-sponsored National Business Conference dinner last Monday. The mining giant awarded the gem to celebrate Botswana's 60-year Independence Anniversary. Chikura, who is from Zimbabwe, had never seen a diamond until this win.

Chikura, a veteran journalist, was assigned to cover the event when she was selected in the draw. Debswana Managing Director Andrew Maatla Motsumi was present. Chikura stated it was an honor and dedicated the diamond to journalists who inform the nation.

She has chosen to keep the diamond's value undisclosed. Chikura previously named her daughter Ruby, a name meaning red gemstone, and finds the win a happy coincidence. She mentioned it is the first time in many years Debswana has given out a diamond.

bw.headline: Three charged with possessing 20 uncut diamonds
bw.dek: Locals George Jeffries, Benjamini Gopolang, and Farai Koitheng appeared in court after a mall ambush.
paragraphs: Three Batswana, George Jeffries, 36, Benjamini Gopolang, 30, and Farai Koitheng, 47, appeared in Extension II Magistrates Court on Monday charged with unlawful possession of 20 uncut diamonds. Police apprehended the trio at The Fields Mall on Friday, October 23, acting on an informant's tip. The suspects were found with the diamonds during a midday sting operation witnessed by shoppers.

Prosecutor Kalako requested the accused be remanded in custody, stating that the weight and value of the diamonds are yet to be determined. Magistrate Kamogelo Mmesi described the allegations as serious and ordered the three to remain in custody for 14 days while police investigations continue. The accused include a purchased and inventory clerk, a mechanic, and an unemployed individual.

The case has generated public interest regarding how the individuals allegedly obtained the diamonds. The prosecution promised to provide further answers at the next court appearance, scheduled for November 9. The police are working to establish the full circumstances surrounding the alleged crime.

bf.headline: Le Cercle Rose raises funds for breast cancer screening
bf.dek: An event in Ouagadougou on October 24, 2026, aimed to fund screening for 100 vulnerable women.
paragraphs: An initiative called "Le Cercle Rose" held a solidarity dinner in Ouagadougou on October 24, 2026, to raise funds for breast cancer screening. The event, led by Djamila Bonkoungou, director general of Zind Naaba Appart Hôtel, brought together health professionals, associations, foundations, and donors. The goal is to provide screening and medical support to 100 vulnerable women.

The "Le Cercle Rose" initiative aims to overcome financial barriers that prevent many women in Burkina Faso from accessing necessary medical examinations. The solidarity dinner served as a platform to discuss early detection and mobilize financial resources. Organizers reported that the fundraising efforts exceeded expectations, though the final amount collected is still being determined as donation pledges are consolidated.

Beyond the initial target of 100 women, the funds raised may also support further investigations for women whose screening reveals anomalies. Professor Charlemagne spoke at the event about the risk factors, prevention, and the critical importance of early detection for improving treatment outcomes in Burkina Faso.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso official sentenced to two months in jail
bf.dek: Lebinoua Nikièma received a 12-month sentence, with two months suspended, and a fine for inciting unrest.
paragraphs: A court in Ouaga I on October 27, 2026, sentenced Lebinoua Nikièma to 12 months in prison, with two months to be served immediately, and a one million CFA franc fine. Nikièma, a financial services administrator, was found guilty of inciting demoralization of the armed forces and outraging public officials. He was acquitted of charges related to undermining state security.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso PM meets diaspora in Moscow
bf.dek: Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo discussed administrative documents and scholarships with Burkinabè citizens in Russia.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo met with Burkinabè citizens living in Moscow on October 30, 2026, during the Russia-Africa summit. Accompanied by three government members and the ambassador, Ouédraogo heard the national anthem sung by attendees. Gaston Millogo, president of the High Council of Burkinabè in Russia, welcomed the delegation and praised efforts for national sovereignty and development.

Millogo stated that the Burkinabè community in Russia reflects resilience and is committed to contributing to Burkina Faso's prosperity. He cited community contributions to water pump installations in Tobinkora in 2019 and Dorokui in 2021. Student representative Kiswensida Salif Kaboré presented requests for easier administrative document acquisition, passport renewals, and scholarship supplements, which the government acknowledged.

Bouraima Sangaré, representing Burkinabè businesspeople, introduced the Russo-Burkinabè Friendship Club, a group of 200 entrepreneurs ready to explore economic cooperation. Prime Minister Ouédraogo emphasized Russia's role as a strategic partner against terrorism and for development, thanking the diaspora for their commitment to Burkina Faso.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso learns from China's targeted poverty fight
bf.dek: Adapting to local realities, China's poverty reduction strategy focuses on specific household needs and resources.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso is examining China's approach to poverty reduction, which emphasizes understanding local conditions like soil, climate, and resources to tailor solutions. This method, known as precise poverty targeting, involves identifying the unique difficulties faced by each household and community rather than applying a one-size-fits-all aid model. The goal is to inspire autonomous development by respecting local particularities.

China's past efforts in remote villages highlight the failure of uniform aid or unsuitable crop introductions, leading to wasted resources and unstable incomes. The strategy begins by directly engaging with villagers to pinpoint specific needs such as lack of water, land, skills, or stable employment. Based on these assessments, appropriate agricultural and economic activities suited to local natural conditions are chosen.

Examples from China include Shibadong village, which leveraged its Miao ethnic heritage for embroidery, rural tourism, and fruit cultivation after improved road access, and Minning, which adapted to its arid climate by developing water-efficient goji berry and grape farming. These cases demonstrate how tailored strategies can lead to sustainable livelihoods and collective poverty escape.

bi.headline: Burundi soldier shoots man smuggling fuel
bi.dek: A man is in critical condition after being shot by a soldier while transporting fuel from the DRC.
paragraphs: A man was critically injured by a gunshot on Thursday evening, October 29, 2026, in Kaburantwa, Bukinanyana commune, Bujumbura province. The victim was riding a motorcycle carrying fuel containers from the Democratic Republic of Congo when a soldier fired at his legs after he refused to stop. He was taken to a health center in Kaburantwa before being transferred to Prince Régent Charles Hospital in Bujumbura.

Local administration stated the soldier shot the man's legs when he did not comply with orders. The fuel enters Burundi from the RDC via the Rusizi River and is collected near the border before being sold illegally. Residents questioned the use of live ammunition, suggesting a warning shot could have been used. This incident occurs amid ongoing tensions between law enforcement and fuel smugglers.

The victim remained in critical condition at the hospital. This event highlights the risks associated with the clandestine fuel trade, which supplies markets in Burundi, including Bujumbura, where prices can be five times the official rate. Burundi has faced fuel shortages for nearly six years, leading some citizens to travel to the RDC for supplies.

bi.headline: Burundi U15 team finishes top 8 in division
bi.dek: The Burundi U15 team reached the quarter-finals of Division D at the FIFA U15 World Cup Festival in Baku.
paragraphs: The Burundi U15 team competed in the first FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan, on October 30, 2026. The tournament featured 189 nations playing football at eight a side. Burundi was placed in Level D, the fourth tier of the competition, which ranked teams from 97th to 128th globally.

Burundi's journey included a 4-3 victory against Togo in the Level D round of 16 and a 2-1 win over Cape Verde in the round of 8. However, their progress was halted by a 7-0 defeat to Canada in the Level D quarter-finals on October 28. Reaching these quarter-finals placed Burundi in the Top 8 of Division D.

Spain was crowned the overall world champion after winning Level A, defeating the Czech Republic in the final. Eight African nations, including Algeria, Morocco, Angola, Cameroon, Guinea, Egypt, Ghana, and Kenya, finished as group leaders. Guinea achieved the best African performance, finishing 6th overall.

bi.headline: PAM equips Burundi institutions with 74 devices
bi.dek: Computers, printers, and scanners will strengthen public services for school feeding and social protection.
paragraphs: The World Food Programme (WFP) provided 74 pieces of equipment, including laptops, printers, and scanners, to Burundi's National Office for Refugees and Stateless Persons (ONPRA) and the Permanent Executive Secretariat of the National Social Protection Commission (SEP/CNPS) on October 30, 2026. The equipment aims to enhance the work capabilities of public services involved in school feeding and social protection initiatives.

Of the total devices, 27 laptops and 27 printers/scanners are allocated to education services in 27 communes, while 14 laptops and 6 printers/scanners will support the social protection sector. This initiative accompanies the increasing responsibility of communes in organizing school meals, with WFP support and under the Ministry of National Education and Scientific Research.

The national school feeding program, PNASE, prioritizes locally produced food, connecting children's education with economic opportunities for agricultural producers and local processing units. Schools will source supplies from cooperatives, fostering a link between education and local economic development.

cm.headline: Cameroon refugee artisans seek wider markets
cm.dek: Over 135 refugees in East Region receive vocational training and access to sales outlets.
paragraphs: More than 135 Central African refugees in Cameroon's East Region have received or are undergoing vocational and business training. The programme, a partnership between Cameroon's Ministry of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) from 2024–2026, offers skills in areas like cassava processing, tailoring, and business management. 10 refugees currently use a permanent exhibition and sales outlet in Bertoua.

The initiative, implemented through the Bertoua Regional Craft Village (VARB), aims to help beneficiaries organise production and reach wider commercial markets. Participating artisans have attended the Cameroon International Handicrafts Exhibition in 2024 and 2026. A refugee craftswoman won the national Art and Decoration award at the 2026 exhibition.

VARB coordinator Alexis Carole Ngassomo Emama Miasse proposed organising artisans by trade to boost production capacity and fulfil orders. UNHCR's Bertoua office and the University of Bertoua organised a dialogue on October 26 and 27 where e-commerce training was also recommended.

cm.headline: Cameroon to raise 2027 public investment budget
cm.dek: The government aims for a significant rise in public investment next year but may miss its 40% budget target.
paragraphs: Cameroon's government plans to raise its public investment budget in 2027, aiming for a significant increase from the current year. However, this rise is still expected to fall short of the National Development Strategy's goal of allocating 40% of the general budget to investment.

The Cabinet acknowledged this gap after a meeting on October 27, 2026, in Yaoundé, chaired by Prime Minister Joseph Dion Ngute. While promising a substantial boost in investment, the statement did not provide specific figures for the proposed allocation or its percentage of the overall budget. This announcement follows a presidential circular from October 12, which set a minimum investment target of 30% for 2027.

In 2026, Cameroon's Public Investment Budget (PIB) is CFA2,031.15 billion, representing 23.4% of the CFA8,683.9 billion general budget. This is 6.6 percentage points below the 2027 minimum target. These figures reflect budgeted amounts, not actual spending, with unfinished projects and electricity prioritized for 2027.

cm.headline: Chinese firm eyes $63.0M sugar, rice investment in Cameroon
cm.dek: Nanning Agricultural Development Group is considering large-scale plantations and a processing complex in Batouri.
paragraphs: Chinese state-owned company Nanning Agricultural Development Group is considering investing approximately CFA88 billion (US$63.03M) in sugar and rice production in Batouri, Cameroon’s East Region. The proposed project includes sugarcane and rice cultivation alongside a factory designed to produce 60,000 tonnes of sugar annually.

The investment remains at the feasibility assessment stage, with the company seeking a specialised consultancy to evaluate the project’s technical and financial viability. Bids for the feasibility study, for which Nanning has allocated up to CFA78 million (US$55.87M), are due by November 5, 2026.

This proposed investment revives plans for a sugar complex in Batouri, where previous initiatives by Justin Sugar Mills and Cosumar failed to reach implementation. Orient’s Sugar and Industry SA also explored developing a sugar complex in the East Region in October 2017.

cm.headline: Cameroon bauxite project awaits CFA36.5 billion loan
cm.dek: AFG Bank Cameroon will inspect the Minim-Martap bauxite site in November before deciding on CFA36.5 billion loan release.
paragraphs: Canyon Resources has not yet secured CFA36.5 billion in bank financing for its Minim-Martap bauxite project in Cameroon's Adamawa region. AFG Bank Cameroon scheduled a site inspection for November 2026 before deciding whether to resume disbursements under the syndicated loan. The bank suspended further withdrawals more than two months after the inspection was originally due.

The bank is awaiting the site visit and a review of the project's development schedule and financial model. Canyon submitted requested documents in the third quarter, but the review is ongoing. Lenders must still approve the project's requirements before releasing additional funds. As of September 30, 2026, Canyon's Cameroon subsidiary, Camalco, had drawn CFA45.5 billion of the CFA82 billion loan.

The syndicated loan was for a total of CFA82 billion. Camalco had drawn 55.5% of the loan as of September 30, 2026. The bank's decision on resuming disbursements is pending the site inspection and review outcomes.

This donation aims to strengthen the monitoring, evaluation, and quality of education across the country.

The equipment, including printing and projection devices, specialized software, and collaborative tools, was provided under the Support Program for the Professionalization of the Teaching Profession in Cameroon (PAPMEC). The Minister of Basic Education (MINEDUB) signed a property transfer agreement during the ceremony, marking a step in enhancing national capacity for educational system coordination and assessment.

This initiative, funded by the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) and implemented by UNESCO and UNICEF, will enable teams to better manage program activities, analyze school achievement data, and inform decisions for improved learning quality. The UNESCO Director emphasized the organization's commitment to supporting member states' efforts in providing inclusive and quality education.

paragraphs: The MLPC Bureau Exécutif in Bangui declared on October 20, 2026, that it disassociates itself from Martin Ziguélé. The party stated Ziguélé was removed as MLPC president by the Congress but continues to act and speak in the party's name without authorization.

The party urged vigilance against these 'criminals' who have previously caused displacement and economic damage. The MLPC has informed administrative and judicial authorities about Ziguélé's actions, asserting he no longer controls the 'real MLPC'.

km.headline: Comoros drafts 2035 migration policy
km.dek: The plan aims to unify migration governance, protect migrants, and leverage diaspora resources for development.
paragraphs: The Comoros government, led by Interior Minister Mohamed Ahmed Assoumani, has presented a draft national migration policy aimed at organizing the country's approach to migration until 2035. This initiative, developed with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), seeks to balance national sovereignty with migrant protection and economic growth.

The policy document, presented by national consultant Moctar Zouboudou, outlines eight objectives including strengthening institutions, legal frameworks, and inter-agency coordination. Key priorities also include protecting migrants' fundamental rights, preventing irregular migration, and combating human trafficking and smuggling, while facilitating safe and regular mobility and organizing returns.

A significant aspect of the policy focuses on the Comorian diaspora, with the government intending to better mobilize their financial resources and skills for national development. Other planned orientations include adapting to climate crises, improving migration data, and enhancing international partnerships.

Ikounga Dikanono, who is close to Edgar Nguesso, replaces Jean-Dominique Okemba, who was dismissed in April.

The new deputy Grand Master also serves as the director of the presidential domain and has gained influence within Congolese Freemasonry. The Grande Loge du Congo is undergoing a reshuffling, with younger Freemasons advancing. Maixent Raoul Ominga, director-general of the national oil company, was named provincial Grand Master for the North. Lawyer Alexis Vincent Gomes remains pro Grand Master.

cg.headline: Congolese civil society seeks say on timber revenue
cg.dek: A new law requires 15% of felled timber to go to the state, but implementation details remain unclear.
paragraphs: Congolese civil society organizations met in Brazzaville from October 29-31, 2026, to scrutinize a new law enacted in October 2024. This law mandates that 15% of all timber felled in the Republic of Congo's forests will directly benefit the state. However, key aspects regarding the management, distribution, and beneficiaries of this state share are yet to be defined in three pending application texts.

The law, stemming from the 2020 Forest Code, transforms the state from a mere tax collector into a co-owner of timber harvests. Forests cover approximately 65% of the Republic of Congo's territory, making timber a significant national resource. Civil society groups, including the Congolese Observatory for Human Rights (OCDH), argue that the law was adopted without sufficient transparency or inclusivity, leaving local communities and indigenous populations uncertain about their share.

Nina Cynthia Kiyindou of OCDH stated that while some representatives participated in the multi-actor text review group (GETMA), broader civil society was not involved. These groups are now preparing recommendations to influence the upcoming application texts, aiming to ensure clarity on how the 15% timber share will be calculated, managed, and utilized for the benefit of Congolese citizens living in forest-dependent communities.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast anti-corruption court investigated for corruption
ci.dek: The FBI alerted Ivorian gendarmes to a corruption network within the economic and financial crimes court in Abidjan.
paragraphs: Ivorian gendarmes are investigating the economic and financial crimes court (PPEF) in Abidjan for corruption, following information provided by the FBI. One person has already been arrested as investigators uncover a network within the specialized court, which handles cases of embezzlement, money laundering, and large-scale fraud. The FBI's involvement stems from American citizens being among the victims of the alleged crimes.

The PPEF is responsible for sensitive cases, including those involving public funds and cybercrime. This investigation comes shortly after the court handed down a 20-year prison sentence and a 100 million CFA franc fine to four young Ivorians in a sextortion case linked to an American woman's suicide in 2022. The convicted individuals are appealing their sentences, and FBI agents were present during that trial.

This development occurs as Ivory Coast was removed from the Financial Action Task Force (GAFI) grey list, a move that acknowledged reforms against money laundering and terrorism financing. The Ministry of Justice has denied accusations of corruption and extortion within the PPEF, stating that the justice system is sound.

Business France aims to "strengthen economic relations between France and West Africa." The results of the mission, including signed contracts or initial contacts, will be known after the Ivory Coast leg concludes on November 4.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast potato imports climb 45% to $12.5 million
ci.dek: Egypt's potato exports to Ivory Coast rose to $1.68 million in 2025, up from $14,000 in 2020.
paragraphs: Ivory Coast spent $12.5 million on fresh or chilled potato imports in the first nine months of 2026, a 45% increase from $8.64 million in the same period of 2025. The country imports an average of 62,000 tonnes of potatoes annually to meet demand that far outstrips its domestic production of less than 100 tons. Imports of processed potato products, including French fries, also rose by 78% from $1.52 million in 2020 to $2.70 million in 2025.

Egypt has become a significant supplier, with its potato shipments to Ivory Coast growing from $14,000 in 2020 to $1.68 million in 2025. This growth is attributed to Egypt's organized logistics network, which includes irrigation, sorting, packaging, phytosanitary inspections, and refrigerated transport. These systems ensure consistent deliveries and minimize losses from farm to market.

Other West African producers show mixed results, with Mali's fresh potato exports to Ivory Coast falling by nearly 92% to $37,000 in the first nine months of 2026, down from $461,000 a year earlier. Senegal is exploring ways to boost its regional potato exports, forecasting over 255,000 tonnes in January 2026. African suppliers must compete on delivery consistency, product quality, and final price to succeed in the Ivorian market.

eg.headline: Bus crash kills three on Red Sea highway
eg.dek: 25 people were injured, including five foreign nationals, when a bus collided with a sand truck.
paragraphs: Three people died, including a bus driver, and 25 others were injured on Friday, October 30, when a passenger bus crashed into a sand-laden truck on the highway between Hurghada and Ras Gharib. The accident occurred approximately 6 miles past Jabal al-Zeit, heading towards Ras Gharib in the Red Sea Governorate.

Local reports indicate the bus struck the truck from behind, partially obstructing traffic, though photographs showed the front of the bus severely damaged. Among the injured were a French citizen, an Italian, and three Russian nationals. Ambulances transported the injured, with conditions ranging from moderate to critical, to nearby hospitals.

Ismail al-Arabi, the Red Sea Governorate’s health undersecretary, visited injured individuals at Ras Gharib Central Hospital, and critical cases were moved to Hurghada General Hospital. Security and traffic officials worked to clear the wreckage and reopen the road, while prosecutors initiated an investigation into the incident.

eg.headline: Egypt shops adjust to winter hours
eg.dek: Retailers will close at 10:00 pm, while restaurants can stay open until midnight.
paragraphs: Egypt's shops and restaurants are now operating under new winter hours following the nation's shift to standard time. Retail shops and malls must close by 10:00 pm, with an extended hour on Thursdays, Fridays, and public holidays. Workshops and craft businesses will operate from eight am to six pm, though exceptions exist for businesses on main roads or providing urgent services.

Restaurants and cafés can welcome customers from five am until midnight, with a one-hour extension to one am on holidays. Home delivery services for these establishments are permitted to operate 24 hours a day. These winter operating hours are distinct from the national time change, which set clocks back by 60 minutes.

Grocery stores, supermarkets, bakeries, fruit and vegetable shops, poultry retailers, wholesale markets, and pharmacies are among the establishments exempted from these closing times. These exemptions allow for continuous operation throughout the night where necessary.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea sets six-month deadline for cocoa factory
gq.dek: The government will launch a cocoa processing factory to produce paste for chocolate.
paragraphs: The government of Equatorial Guinea has given itself six months to launch a factory for processing national cocoa production. This factory will produce cocoa paste, a raw material for chocolate.

The decision was made in Malabo during a meeting with the prime minister and ministers of Agriculture, Hacienda, and Tesorería. Companies ANONEY SERVICE and GETRANSCAO will supply quicklime and copper sulfate, with prices negotiated down by up to 10%. The government will also directly hire a shipping company for transport.

This initiative aims to move Equatorial Guinea from selling raw cocoa to processing its own production. The strategy seeks to strengthen the agricultural sector, improve cocoa and coffee production, create jobs, add value, and reduce reliance on imports.

er.headline: US lifts sanctions on Eritrea
er.dek: Sanctions removed on September 19, 2026, targeted the ruling party's financial and military apparatus.
paragraphs: The United States removed sanctions on Eritrea on September 19, 2026. These sanctions were imposed in 2021 due to Eritrea’s involvement in the Tigray War. The US government had outlined plans to lift the sanctions four months prior, according to a Reuters report.

Human rights groups criticized the decision, citing Eritrea's record of forced labor and torture under the ruling People’s Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ). Eritrea's government called the sanctions 'illicit and immoral' and claimed they caused 'incalculable damage' and constrained development.

The removed sanctions targeted the PFDJ’s financial and military bodies and two officials, Abraha Kassa and Hagos Gebrehiwet. The Eritrean Defence Force’s chief of staff, Filipos Woldeyohannes, remains under separate sanctions. The PFDJ has previously benefited from the removal of UN sanctions in 2018, remaining self-sufficient.

ke.headline: Kenya threatens Africa CDC action over Saudi travel ban
ke.dek: Nairobi protests disproportionate Ebola travel restrictions that suspend visas and bar arrivals.
paragraphs: Kenya's Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs has threatened to escalate its concerns over Saudi Arabia’s suspension of travel from Kenya to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC). The ministry described the restrictions, which include suspending visa issuance and barring travellers who have been in Kenya within the previous 21 days, as disproportionate and potentially harmful to Kenya’s economic and diplomatic interests.

The ministry, headed by Musalia Mudavadi, stated on October 30 that it would work with other affected African countries to present the matter to Africa CDC. Kenya argues that restrictions not supported by scientific evidence could set a concerning precedent for the continent. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Health maintain that Kenya has contained the Ebola outbreak, with no new cases reported since October 19.

Saudi Arabia suspended travel by its citizens to Kenya and stopped issuing visas over Ebola concerns. Kenya is demanding Saudi Arabia review and lift the measures, challenging the kingdom to submit scientific justification to the World Health Organization. Seven patients receiving treatment are expected to be discharged on November 3.

ke.headline: Sifuna demands transparency on Mrima Hills mining project
ke.dek: Linda Mwananchi Movement party leader questions benefits for Kwale residents from rare earth mineral extraction.
paragraphs: Linda Mwananchi Movement party leader Edwin Sifuna has demanded full disclosure of the proposed Mrima Hills mining project in Kwale. Sifuna stated that all mining agreements and contracts should be made public, arguing that communities in mineral-rich areas must know the terms under which investors operate and how benefits will be shared. The project involves extracting niobium and rare earth minerals, used in aerospace, electronics, and electric vehicle manufacturing.

Sifuna questioned what had been agreed between the government and prospective investors, insisting residents have a right to know the proposed arrangements. He raised concerns over land ownership, compensation, and revenue sharing, warning that residents could lose land without adequate compensation. Mining Cabinet Secretary Hassan Joho stated that five bidders submitted proposals on October 21, 2026, and the government expects to award the project within two to three weeks.

The mineral deposit is believed to contain tens of billions of dollars’ worth of rare earth minerals and niobium. Sifuna’s concerns follow previous operations in Kwale where Base Titanium operated for over a decade, with Sifuna claiming communities did not receive promised benefits. Two American consortia, a US-linked group, an Australian consortium, and a Kenyan-British joint venture are among the five contenders.

ke.headline: Taita Taveta targets US$4.3 million potato industry growth
ke.dek: The county government is improving access to certified seeds, farmer training, and market linkages to boost production.
paragraphs: Taita Taveta County aims to grow its Irish potato industry, currently worth US$4.3 million annually, by increasing production from its 750 hectares. The county government is implementing measures to boost farmers' incomes and create jobs, particularly for young people.

The county's 750 hectares yield an estimated 11,250 tonnes of potatoes annually, with average productivity at 15 tonnes per hectare. Farm-gate prices average US$0.39 per kilogram, offering economic opportunities. The government is improving access to certified seeds and farmer training through initiatives like Farmer Field and Business Schools, which have supported 21 farmer groups.

Nine half-acre demonstration plots have been established to train farmers in improved production techniques. Agripreneur Gift Kisombe connected farmers with a seed supplier who purchased certified Markies seed potatoes worth US$1,010. The Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization is identifying potato varieties suited to the county's diverse ecological zones.

ke.headline: First body recovered from Nairobi building collapse
ke.dek: 16 people remain missing after an 18-storey building collapsed in Nairobi last Friday.
paragraphs: A woman's body was recovered Friday from the rubble of an 18-storey building that collapsed a week ago in Nairobi's Eastleigh district, as 16 people remain missing.

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja stated the building lacked required construction permits and that renting ground and basement floors before an occupancy certificate was illegal. Families have gathered at the site for a week, with hopes fading after the critical 72-hour survival window passed.

Thermal imaging cameras, supplied by a Chinese team, are being used in the search, having previously detected two individuals beneath the debris. No survivors have been rescued since Saturday, though four people were previously pulled from the wreckage.

za.dek: President Ramaphosa urged Limpopo to deliver over 90% of votes in the November 4 local government elections.
paragraphs: The African National Congress (ANC) in Limpopo faces pressure to achieve President Cyril Ramaphosa's goal of over 90% of the vote in the local government elections on November 4. Provincial leaders, including chair Phophi Ramathuba, have been campaigning across the province to secure this target. Ramaphosa had previously expressed his expectation for Limpopo to deliver higher numbers than the 70% received in the 2024 elections.

Provincial chair Phophi Ramathuba urged voters to cast their ballots for the ANC, referencing the sacrifices of past leaders like Oliver Tambo. ANC provincial spokesperson Tony Rachoene stated the party views the 90% target as a challenge to intensify campaign efforts, aiming to win all wards and municipalities. He expressed confidence in achieving a decisive majority due to strong internal unity and support mobilisation.

The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party leader Jacob Zuma released a video urging South Africans to vote in the November 4 elections, stating his party is ready to govern. Zuma is expected to address supporters at KwaMashu on November 1. Political analyst Solly Rashilo suggested the 90% target might be ambitious, noting that municipal elections are influenced by service delivery and local dissatisfaction.

za.headline: Simon Harmer leads South Africa to series win
za.dek: Spin bowler Simon Harmer took career-best figures of 6/16 in the final innings to secure a 176-run victory against Australia.
paragraphs: Spin bowler Simon Harmer played a key role for South Africa in Cape Town on Saturday, taking career-best figures of 6/16 in Australia’s second innings. The 37-year-old’s performance helped the Proteas to a 176-run victory in the Test series decider at Newlands, securing a 2-1 series win. Harmer also achieved 10 wickets in the match for the first time in a five-day game, earning him the Player of the Match award.

Harmer, playing in his 17th test, credited his lengthy domestic career experience for his performance, stating he focused on dealing with expectations. He had struggled in the first two matches of the series, taking only two wickets in each. "It’s been a tough few weeks but I will enjoy tonight," Harmer said after the match. The Proteas secured their first Test series victory over Australia since 2018.

South Africa scored 329 in their first innings, with contributions from Marques Ackerman (95) and Aiden Markram (78), before Australia replied with 429, led by Josh Inglis (102). The Proteas then posted 387 in their second innings, featuring centuries from Wiaan Mulder (115) and Ryan Rickelton (101), setting Australia a target of 288. Australia were bowled out for 111 in their second innings on October 31, 2026.

za.headline: The Kiffness shows Johannesburg decline
za.dek: Musician David Scott shared a video comparing Johannesburg in 2010 to 2026, highlighting infrastructure decay.
paragraphs: Musician David Scott, known as The Kiffness, has released a video showing the rapid deterioration of Johannesburg over 15 years. The 38-year-old artist used Google Street View images from 2010 and 2026 to illustrate the city's decline, comparing well-maintained streets then to neglected buildings and rubbish-strewn roads now.

Scott shared the video on X after a Polymarket report claimed Johannesburg was on the "brink of a total collapse" due to water shortages from damaged infrastructure. He stated his intention was to show how a functioning city can become derelict quickly, warning other major global cities of a similar fate if they do not act.

Johannesburg voters will elect councillors on Wednesday, November 4, during local government elections. A Polymarket poll indicates Helen Zille has a 57% chance of becoming the next mayor, with her campaign focusing on restoring basic services, infrastructure, financial management, and combating crime and corruption.

za.headline: Helen Zille warns Joburg voters against election boycott
za.dek: The DA's Johannesburg mayoral candidate urged voters to cast ballots on November 4 to prevent corruption.
paragraphs: Democratic Alliance mayoral candidate Helen Zille warned Johannesburg voters on Saturday, October 31, that staying away from the November 4 polls risks allowing corrupt officials another five years in power. Speaking at the DA's final rally in Mamelodi, Tshwane, Zille urged frustrated residents to vote rather than boycott, stating that not voting rewards the politicians they wish to hold accountable.

Zille argued that Johannesburg cannot endure another five years of failed governance and highlighted her five-point plan to address service delivery issues. Her pledges include fixing potholes within 72 hours, ensuring 95% of traffic lights function, and restoring water and electricity supplies. The plan also aims to tackle corruption and professionalize the city's administration.

Johannesburg is a key battleground for Wednesday's local government elections, with issues like water outages and failing infrastructure dominating the debate. Approved special voters will cast ballots on November 2 and 3, ahead of the general election on November 4.

za.headline: Into the Woods musical opens in Cape Town
za.dek: Sondheim's dark fairy tale reimagining features 25 student performers at the Theatre on the Bay.
paragraphs: A new production of the musical Into the Woods, a reimagining of fairy tales by Sondheim and James Lapine, has opened at Cape Town's Theatre on the Bay. Directed by Sylvaine Strike, the show features a cast of 25 students from the Lamta musical theatre academy.

The production brings to life classic fairy tale elements including a Giant, a Wolf, Jack and the beanstalk, a Witch, and two princes. Actors use blackened planks to represent the dark, perilous woods, creating an interactive and dynamic forest setting.

The show revisits darker, pre-Disney versions of tales attributed to the Brothers Grimm, with characters like Cinderella and Rapunzel receiving modern updates. Cinderella's stepsisters' feet are described as being mutilated in an attempt to fit the slipper.

ng.headline: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control confirms negative Ebola tests
ng.dek: Two suspected cases in Adamawa State tested negative for Ebola Virus Disease after two rounds of laboratory tests.
paragraphs: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) announced that two suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases in Adamawa State have tested negative. The individuals, who showed symptoms suggestive of Ebola in Yola, were isolated while investigations took place. The NCDC confirmed that the index case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) remains the only confirmed infection in Nigeria.

NCDC Director-General Dr Jide Idris stated that the report of the suspected cases was received by the Adamawa State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) on October 30, 2026. Samples from the individuals underwent two rounds of laboratory testing, both yielding negative results for Ebola. Idris commended the Adamawa State Commissioner for Health and their team for their proactive approach and assured continued technical support.

This development follows the confirmation of a Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja, involving a traveler from Uganda. The negative results in Adamawa have eased concerns about a potential spread. Idris urged the public to remain calm and avoid spreading unverified information, advising them to seek official communication channels for updates. He also stressed the importance of continued vigilance and seeking immediate medical attention for anyone experiencing Ebola-like symptoms.

ng.headline: Group urges southern presidency until 2031
ng.dek: BTO For PBAT '27 Support Group says power rotation promotes equity and political balance in Nigeria.
paragraphs: The BTO For PBAT ’27 Support Group has called for the Nigerian presidency to remain in Southern Nigeria until 2031. Director-General Ogbeni Adojutelegan Adesuyi Gideon stated in Akure that this would promote equity, fairness, and political balance. He argued that allowing the South to complete an eight-year tenure would strengthen national unity and democratic stability.

Adojutelegan acknowledged that power rotation is not in the constitution but is a vital political arrangement for national cohesion. The group, led by the Minister of Interior Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, believes equitable arrangements are essential for mutual trust and deepening democracy. They stated their position is anchored on equity, fairness, and justice, not sectionalism.

The group advocates for the continuation of a southern presidency until 2031 to reinforce fairness and political accommodation. They stressed that Nigeria's democratic stability depends on leaders upholding inclusion and mutual respect. This call is for political fairness and democratic consolidation, not to deny any Nigerian the right to contest elections.

ng.headline: Nigeria cocoa exports to US jump 554%
ng.dek: Shipments reached $142 million in 2025, up from $21.7 million the previous year, according to the US Mission in Nigeria.
paragraphs: Nigeria's cocoa bean exports to the United States surged by 554.4% to $142 million in 2025, a significant increase from $21.7 million in 2024. The United States Mission in Nigeria announced these figures, highlighting growing trade between the two nations.

The mission stated that US demand for Nigerian cocoa is booming, with exports to the United States rising sharply. This growth in trade occurs as Nigeria aims to diversify its foreign exchange earnings and boost agricultural production.

Despite the export surge, Nigeria's cocoa industry faces challenges including old plantations, limited financing, and low productivity. Over 80% of Nigeria's cocoa is exported raw, limiting local value addition and job creation.

et.headline: Drone strikes kill 25 civilians in Ethiopia
et.dek: Witnesses report multiple drone attacks in Amhara and Tigray regions since Thursday, hitting a camp for displaced people.
paragraphs: At least 25 civilians, including children, died in drone strikes across Ethiopia's northern regions starting Thursday. Witnesses and a medical source reported the deaths on Friday. The Ethiopian government has been using drones in its conflict with rebels in Amhara and Tigray states.

In Amhara, four drone strikes hit a camp for displaced people on Thursday, according to one witness. Yasin, who requested anonymity, stated that 14 people were buried at the camp and two more died during medical treatment, with children and pregnant women among the victims. Other residents reported 14 and 15 deaths, including several children.

The strikes occurred near Addis Ababa, approximately 400 kilometers northeast of the capital, as students were returning from school. One witness described the dismemberment of his sister-in-law's body. At least 22 others were injured in repeated strikes on shelters housing families displaced by the conflict.

et.headline: Ethiopian gunfire heard as thousands flee into Kenya
et.dek: Over 36,000 people have crossed into Kenya from Ethiopia due to ongoing fighting.
paragraphs: Gunfire was heard from Ethiopia into Kenya's town of Moyale on Friday morning as civilians fled violence. An Associated Press journalist recorded the sounds on October 30. The United Nations reported that 36,000 people had crossed into Kenya by Tuesday.

The influx of refugees, mostly women and children, is due to fighting near Moyale, according to the UN. Benedict Munywoki, deputy county commissioner for Moyale Sub-County, stated that more people are fleeing Ethiopia into Kenya. Aid agencies including the UN refugee agency, International Organization for Migration, and Kenya Red Cross are providing medical care, food, and shelter.

An Ethiopian doctor, Seifu Negash, who fled to Kenya, is volunteering with the Kenya Red Cross to treat refugees. The conflict on the Ethiopian side involves a territorial dispute between Oromia and Somali regional administrations, exacerbated by the killing of a 13-year-old girl. Local leaders in Kenya's Marsabit County are seeking support, concerned that the arrivals could strain resources amid existing food and water shortages.

gh.dek: Police arrested a woman and seek Samuel Osei Anto for the Friday, October 30, 2026, double murder.
paragraphs: Irene Atubiga, 47, CEO of Kussa Shea Bliss, and her 57-year-old uncle George Atubiga were shot dead at their NTHC Estate home in Sakumono, Accra on Friday, October 30, 2026. The killings followed a dispute over a GH¢500,000 loan George Atubiga allegedly owed to suspect Samuel Christopher Osei Anto. Police have arrested Beatrice Mumuni in connection with the incident.

According to the Ghana Police Service, Samuel Osei Anto, accompanied by Beatrice Mumuni, went to the victims' residence to demand repayment of the loan. A misunderstanding reportedly escalated, leading Osei Anto to shoot and kill both George and Irene Atubiga. Officers found the victims with gunshot wounds, and they were pronounced dead at a hospital.

Kussa Shea Bliss, founded by Irene Atubiga, sources shea butter from women’s cooperatives in Northern Ghana to support their economic empowerment. The company develops premium skincare and personal care products for customers in Ghana and internationally. Police have declared Samuel Christopher Osei Anto a wanted man.

gh.headline: Ghana government funds mother's travel to son's New York funeral
gh.dek: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced the government will cover all costs for Madam Doris Adu Gyamfi to attend the service.
paragraphs: The Government of Ghana will pay for Madam Doris Adu Gyamfi, mother of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong, to travel to New York for her son's funeral. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced this on X on Saturday, October 31, 2026, after New York City Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani and US President Donald Trump intervened to secure a visa for her. The minister stated that the government considered it important for Madam Gyamfi to be present to pay her last respects to her son, Javits, who was shot dead in the Bronx on October 29, 2026.

Minister Ablakwa confirmed he spoke with Madam Gyamfi on Friday and assigned officials to help with her visa application, describing her grief as unimaginable. He added that the Mahama administration would also support a dignified funeral for Javits and continue working to secure justice for him. Javits, a Ghanaian student, had moved to the United States about a year prior to join his father, Thomas Frimpong, who suspects the shooting may be linked to school bullying.

The government's support announcement followed Mayor Mamdani's statement that President Trump would facilitate an immediate visa for Madam Gyamfi after a telephone conversation. Investigations into the shooting are ongoing, with no arrests announced. Madam Gyamfi is expected to travel to New York in the coming days.

paragraphs: Joseph Kofi Assempah, CEO of Assempahfie Graphics, received the CEO of the Year – Print award at the 5th Ghana CEO Vision and Awards. The event took place on October 29 and 30, 2026, at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City in Accra.

gh.headline: Ghana wins financial gold war but loses environmental one
gh.dek: An associate professor says the Ghana Gold Board mobilises gold to support the economy and stabilise the Cedi.
paragraphs: An Associate Professor at the University of Ghana School of Law, Prof Kwadwo Appiagyei-Tuah, stated that Ghana is winning the financial war through gold mobilisation but losing the environmental war due to illegal mining. He praised the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) for its efforts in supporting the economy and stabilising the Ghanaian cedi.

Prof Appiagyei-Tuah highlighted the tension between economic gains from gold and environmental damage, including polluted water bodies and destroyed forest reserves. He acknowledged some progress in fighting illegal mining but questioned the evidence behind reported success figures, noting that some data still indicates alarming levels of the activity.

These comments were made on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 31, amid renewed public debate on government interventions against illegal mining. The professor suggested that while some available information points to government progress, other figures do not support this assessment.

gh.headline: National Theatre to host Funworld 2026
gh.dek: The fifth edition of Funworld will use performing arts to promote mental health awareness and breast cancer education.
paragraphs: The National Theatre of Ghana will host Funworld 2026, an event combining education, entertainment, and competition to raise awareness of mental well-being and breast cancer among schoolchildren and the community. This October edition is part of the National Theatre’s use of the arts for social awareness and children’s development. For over three decades, Funworld has served as an edutainment platform for young people to develop and showcase their creative abilities.

This year's event will feature traditional and contemporary dances, drama, poetry, and music performances celebrating Ghanaian culture. A debate competition between Springfield School and Gloryhill International will highlight pupils' public speaking and critical-thinking skills. Promasidor Ghana, through its Twisco product, is partnering with the National Theatre to support the programme.

The programme will emphasize mental health, emotional well-being, and supportive environments for children. Educational messages and artistic presentations will also encourage appreciation for breast cancer awareness and health consciousness. Separately, Kiddafest 2026, also sponsored by Promasidor Ghana, is scheduled for December 17 and 18.

cd.headline: DR Congo boxers win eight African titles
cd.dek: Congolese women secured all eight of their final matches at the amateur boxing championship held in Kinshasa.
paragraphs: The Democratic Republic of Congo has excelled at the amateur boxing Championship of Africa, hosted in Kinshasa from October 19 to November 1, 2026. Congolese female boxers achieved a perfect record, winning all eight of their finals. Several Congolese male boxers also secured continental titles.

Sulamite Tshimwanga won the over 81 kg category, while Déborah Boisabu defeated Zambia's Catherine Mwape in the 52-54 kg division. Ruth Yamfu beat Cameroon's Paule Alliance in the 54-57 kg category. Bénédicte Diyoka earned her second African title in the 45-48 kg final against Bénie Ndoudi of Congo-Brazzaville. Munga Zalia Modestie also claimed the 57-60 kg title after previous silver and bronze medals.

Merveille Mbalayi, Monique Bampala, and Jorbelle Malewu also contributed to the medal haul, defeating opponents from Senegal and Cameroon. In the men's finals, Kolongo Gloire beat Cape Verde's David Daniel Pina in the 51-54 kg category, and Beny Njibu Njibu won the 60-63.5 kg title against Cape Verde's Kevin Admolson.

cd.headline: DR Congo campaign finds 43 suspected cancer cases
cd.dek: Health workers screened 113 women and raised awareness among nearly 600 people in South and North Kivu.
paragraphs: Health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo identified 43 suspected cases of breast and cervical cancer during an October campaign in South and North Kivu provinces. The initiative, led by the Bunyakiri health zone and the Clubs des filles reporters, also provided free consultations to 113 women and raised awareness among over 580 people across three health zones.

Simon Mihona, coordinator for the Clubs des filles reporters, reported that 421 people were informed in Bunyakiri, 90 in Kalonge, and 25 community leaders in Itebero. Medical staff conducted 61 consultations in Bunyakiri, 29 in Itebero, and 23 in Kalonge, leading to the identification of the 43 potential cases, including one probable case in Bunyakiri.

Dr. Marquis Chiralo, head of the Bunyakiri health zone, stated that individuals with suspicious signs require further examinations to confirm or rule out cancer. He urged partners and donors to support such actions, while Kasese Maene, head of the Gender and Family office in Bunyakiri, called for more resources to ensure women receive accurate health status checks.

cd.headline: Kolwezi residents protest Ruashi Mining pollution
cd.dek: Residents of Dilungu and Bel Air neighbourhoods cite health problems and property damage, demanding compensation.
paragraphs: Residents of Dilungu and Bel Air in Kolwezi, Lualaba province, demonstrated on Friday, October 30, to protest environmental and health issues they attribute to Ruashi Mining's operations. They are seeking reparations for damages including cracks in their homes, dried-up crops, and increased health ailments.

The protesters marched to the company's facilities and submitted a memorandum detailing their grievances. They stated they have been alerting authorities to their situation since October 2025 without a satisfactory response. The memorandum specifically mentions cracked homes, damaged roofs, and withered plantations as consequences of the mining activities.

The residents also reported an increase in respiratory illnesses, skin irritations, and nosebleeds. They expressed deep concern and called for serious investigations to determine causes and responsibilities. The protesters regret the lack of concrete measures from authorities despite their repeated efforts since October 2025.

cd.headline: DR Congo families urged to rebuild state values
cd.dek: Professor Dezzy Mukebayi calls for civic and moral values to be taught within families to strengthen the nation.
paragraphs: The reconstruction of the Congolese state must begin within families, stated Professor Dezzy Mukebayi, dean of the Faculty of Law at the Official University of Mbuji-Mayi. He spoke at the 6th interdisciplinary colloquium in Ngandajika, Lomami province, urging parents to transmit civic and moral values to their children. Mukebayi highlighted that Congolese families are weakened by socio-economic crises and insecurity, hindering their ability to teach respect, responsibility, integrity, sharing, and solidarity.

Professor Mukebayi described the family as the primary space where children learn societal rules and civic values, calling it a political and civic space. He encouraged parents to set good examples and appealed to public authorities to better support families in their educational mission. Nancy Ngalula, founder of the NGO ADAAYE, added that restoring cultural and moral values is essential for national identity, noting the urgency to rehabilitate dignity and social cohesion due to observed violence within families.

The colloquium focused on the family as a pillar for rebuilding the Congolese state. Professor Mukebayi's call for state support for families' educational roles and Ngalula's emphasis on restoring cultural values aim to address the societal challenges affecting the nation's foundation.

tz.headline: Kenyan court orders police to produce missing Tanzanian activist
tz.dek: Justice Alexander Muasya Muteti ordered police to present Twaha Mwaipaya in court on November 2, 2026, with a detention warrant.
paragraphs: Kenyan police have been ordered by the High Court in Nairobi to produce missing Tanzanian activist Twaha Mwaipaya before the Milimani High Court on November 2, 2026. Justice Alexander Muasya Muteti issued the order on October 30, requiring authorities to present Mwaipaya with any detention warrant and explain why he should not be released. The directive follows an urgent application by the human-rights organisation Vocal Africa, which is suing on behalf of Mwaipaya after his reported abduction in Kamulu on October 25.

The court directed the Inspector General of Police, the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, and the Officer Commanding Ruai Police Station to produce Mwaipaya "live or dead." The order also requires Inspector General Douglas Kanja Kirocho and DCI Director Amin Mohamed Ibrahim to explain the alleged arrest and detention. Vocal Africa's application also sought preservation of CCTV, tracking records, and an independent investigation into the incident.

This habeas corpus direction aims to protect individuals from arbitrary loss of liberty, as guaranteed by Kenya's Constitution. The court's immediate focus is on Mwaipaya's production and the respondents' replies before the November 2 hearing. Mwaipaya's whereabouts and condition remain unconfirmed as of October 30, with no public reports indicating his release or appearance in court.

tz.headline: Tanzania mourns historian John Iliffe
tz.dek: Professor John Iliffe, who died on August 20, 2026, significantly shaped Tanzanian history studies.
paragraphs: Professor John Iliffe, a historian renowned for his work on Africa, particularly Tanzania, passed away on August 20, 2026. Iliffe joined the University College, Dar es Salaam's history department in 1965, shortly after completing his PhD on German colonialism in Tanganyika. He co-directed a project collecting oral memories of the Maji Maji rebellion across southern Tanzania.

Iliffe's prolific writing covered diverse subjects, including Africa's poor, the HIV/AIDS epidemic, capitalists, and ruling elites. His book 'Africans: The History of a Continent' is a widely used introductory text, with its fourth edition completed just before his death. He was among foreign historians brought to the new department by its first head, Terence Ranger.

The Tanzania National Archives in Dar es Salaam noted Iliffe's frequent use of its documents, with his signature appearing on research sheets from the 1960s and 70s. President Julius Nyerere had called for historians to use oral traditions, a call Iliffe joined by collecting local historical knowledge.

tz.headline: Tanzania opens new government city in Dodoma
tz.dek: President Samia Suluhu Hassan inaugurated the Mtumba Government City, a project costing Sh700 billion.
paragraphs: Tanzania's capital city, Dodoma, has officially opened its new Government City in Mtumba, inaugurated by President Samia Suluhu Hassan on October 30, 2026. This move fulfills a vision initiated in 1973 to establish Dodoma as the nation's administrative and development hub. The new city signifies modern governance and national direction, aiming to align with 21st-century needs and foster investment, trade, and international cooperation.

The Mtumba Government City project, which began its second phase of construction in 2021, involved an investment of approximately Sh700 billion. The development includes about 59 kilometers of roads and modern communication systems, consolidating key government institutions into a central administrative center. This move is intended to enhance public institution efficiency and streamline government operations within a single hub.

Dr. Norga Komba, a member of the Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) Political Committee in China, views the opening as a tangible outcome of long-term vision and a developmental legacy for current and future Tanzanians. The relocation of government activities to Dodoma, strengthened in 2016 and largely completed by 2019, represents a new chapter in Tanzania's governance history.

tz.headline: Tanzania election victims await justice one year on
tz.dek: Thousands may have died in protests after the October 29 election, with many victims still traumatised and seeking redress.
paragraphs: One year after Tanzania's October 29 election, victims of the ensuing violence are still awaiting justice and struggling with trauma. President Samia Suluhu Hassan won the election with 98 percent of the vote after most opposition parties were excluded, leading to protests that security forces suppressed. Rights groups claim thousands died, while a government commission reported 518 deaths.

Twaha Bomeza, a 61-year-old from Dar es Salaam, lost an eye and four teeth during a shootout on election day, leaving him with an internal eye wound, shortness of breath, and constant headaches. He requires surgery for his injuries but cannot afford it. The Catholic Church held masses to honour victims, and the main opposition party, Chadema, observed a seven-day mourning period.

Government critics continue to face fear of abduction, arbitrary arrest, and charges of treason or terrorism. Bomeza expressed his pain, stating, "My blood was spilled here, but a year has passed, and there is no more blood here."

tz.headline: Tanzania and Russia explore new trade and investment opportunities
tz.dek: Engineer Mashauri Jofrey Sabwoya highlights potential for economic and technological cooperation following recent high-level visits.
paragraphs: Tanzania and Russia are entering a new phase of relations, with opportunities in trade, investment, education, science, technology, energy, agriculture, and industry identified as key areas for cooperation. These potential benefits stem from recent diplomatic engagements, including President Samia Suluhu Hassan's visit to Russia in June 2026 and Prime Minister Dr. Mwigulu Nchemba's participation in the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow in October 2026.

Engineer Mashauri Jofrey Sabwoya, who serves as the Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) Diaspora Secretary in Russia and Chairman of the Tanzania Students' Federation there, believes these high-level meetings open doors for enhanced collaboration. He emphasizes the need to translate these diplomatic efforts into tangible benefits for Tanzanian citizens, moving beyond mere agreements and discussions.

Sabwoya noted that the historical relationship between Tanzania and Russia, which began with support for liberation movements, now has the potential to evolve into a partnership yielding direct advantages for the populace. He specifically pointed to the opportunities in sectors such as mining, industry, and technology as areas where Russia's experience and knowledge could accelerate Tanzania's development.

ma.headline: Morocco's Nador West Med port attracts $5.5 billion investment
ma.dek: The Nador West Med complex aims to become a key maritime, industrial, and energy hub connecting Europe and Africa.
paragraphs: Morocco's Nador West Med port complex has secured 54 billion dirhams ($5.5 billion) in public and private investment. Forbes reported this investment strengthens the country's goal to become a major maritime, industrial, and energy hub linking Europe and Africa. The first phase of its main container terminal is nearing operation, reflecting King Mohammed VI’s infrastructure strategy.

The port is designed to expand Morocco’s international trade role and benefit from global supply chain shifts. Its energy infrastructure includes a hydrocarbon terminal for 25 million tonnes annually and a planned liquefied natural gas terminal to process five billion cubic meters yearly. These facilities could bolster Morocco's energy security and industrial growth.

Forbes stated the port complex could reinforce Morocco's position as a link between European energy demand and African markets. The project is also expected to stimulate economic activity in Morocco’s eastern region through industrial investment and logistics services. Crown Prince Moulay El Hassan launched operations at the first container terminal on Saturday, October 31.

ma.headline: Morocco sees UN Sahara file closure after MINURSO mandate failure
ma.dek: Government spokesperson Samir Belfqih stated that Russia's veto of a UN resolution marks a new phase in the dispute.
paragraphs: Morocco's government declared Saturday that the UN's failure to renew MINURSO's mandate is a significant step toward closing the Sahara dispute at the United Nations. This development followed Russia's veto of a US-backed Security Council resolution.

Government spokesperson Samir Belfqih said the outcome reflects growing international support for Morocco’s sovereignty over its southern provinces and its autonomy initiative. He stated that the Royal Cabinet’s statement signals a new phase in the dispute, building on diplomatic momentum under King Mohammed VI.

Belfqih described MINURSO's 35-year presence as part of an outdated international framework, noting the diplomatic environment has changed since the mission's 1991 establishment. He reaffirmed Morocco's commitment to the ceasefire and continued development in the southern provinces.

ug.headline: Jubilee Insurance cleans Kampala streets
ug.dek: Company staff joined city officials in a cleanup exercise to prevent disease spread and flooding.
paragraphs: Jubilee Insurance Uganda employees participated in a city cleaning exercise on Saturday alongside Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA) officials. The cleanup covered streets including Kimathi Avenue, Parliament Avenue, and Kampala Road, aiming to improve sanitation and reduce disease risks.

Jubilee Insurance chief executive officer Eugine Mutekhele stated that regular cleaning and proper waste management are critical to reducing the spread of diseases like malaria, typhoid, and cholera, which disproportionately affect low-income communities. He emphasized that preventive care is better than curative, urging other corporations to support the government's monthly cleaning initiative.

KCCA officials noted that the monthly cleaning program has not yet attracted widespread participation and appealed for more organisations to provide equipment and mobilize residents. Sheila Komugisha, KCCA woman councillor, thanked Jubilee Insurance and called for sustained cooperation between authorities, businesses, and communities to improve sanitation.

ug.headline: Uganda Tourism Board partners with CAF for AFCON 2027 promotion
ug.dek: The "Explore Uganda – The Pearl of Africa" brand will feature in tournament promotions to attract visitors.
paragraphs: Uganda has secured destination sponsorship rights for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) through an agreement between the Uganda Tourism Board (UTB) and the Confederation of African Football (CAF). This partnership will promote Uganda's tourism attractions to football supporters, teams, officials, and media attending the continental tournament. The TotalEnergies CAF AFCON PAMOJA 2027 will be co-hosted by Uganda, Kenya, and Tanzania from June 19 to July 17, 2027.

The deal was announced in Kampala, with CAF General Secretary Samson Adamu stating that Uganda can leverage football's popularity to position itself as a tourism destination. UTB Chief Executive Officer Juliana Kagwa called the event the biggest tourism marketing opportunity for Uganda in a generation, aiming to showcase wildlife, culture, and hospitality. The partnership was launched with the attendance of Tourism Minister Tom Butime and Minister of State for Sports Peter Ogwang.

The agreement aims to expose Uganda's attractions to over 3 billion global viewers of the AFCON. CAF is working with Uganda, Kenya, and Tanzania to build ties with the business community. The "Explore Uganda – The Pearl of Africa" brand will be visible through broadcast, digital, and in-stadium platforms, encouraging visitors to explore beyond matches.
