ug.headline: Austrian diplomat warns of trust erosion over Uganda court delays
ug.dek: Dr Katja Kerschbaumer stated that prolonged trials and torture risk undermining public confidence in Uganda's institutions.
paragraphs: Dr Katja Kerschbaumer, head of the Austrian Embassy, warned that lengthy court proceedings and torture are damaging public trust in Uganda's institutions. Speaking at a governance review meeting in Kampala, she emphasized that timely justice and adherence to constitutional rights are vital for national stability and public confidence. Kerschbaumer stated that justice delayed can become justice denied, affecting individuals, families, and businesses.

The diplomat expressed concern over suspects spending excessive time in custody awaiting trial, noting that fundamental rights, including protection from torture, cannot be suspended. She highlighted that while some rights can be limited for public interest, such as land acquisition for infrastructure, these must be lawful, transparent, and proportionate. Kerschbaumer praised Uganda's constitution for its protections but stressed that citizens must believe institutions are fair and impartial.

Kerschbaumer noted that when citizens trust institutions, social cohesion, cooperation, and stability are enhanced. She was speaking on behalf of the Justice Sector Development Partners Group during the Fifth Annual Governance and Security Programme Review meeting.

ug.headline: Uganda targets higher coffee export earnings
ug.dek: A new African Union strategy aims to boost local processing and continental trade for coffee.
paragraphs: Uganda aims to increase coffee export earnings by focusing on local processing and expanded continental trade, reducing reliance on raw bean exports. This initiative follows figures showing African coffee producers earn less than US$3 billion annually from a global market exceeding US$465 billion. The African Union has designated coffee as a strategic commodity to help producers capture more value through processing, roasting, packaging, and direct market access.

Inter-African Coffee Organisation (IACO) Secretary-General Ambassador Solomon Rutega shared these figures with Uganda’s Chargé d’Affaires in Ethiopia, Margaret Kafeero, in Addis Ababa. Rutega stated that processing coffee locally could raise its value from US$2 per kilogram of raw beans to US$40 per kilogram of finished products. This transformation could improve the livelihoods of over 10 million households across Africa dependent on coffee production.

The strategy aligns with Uganda's efforts to boost domestic processing, create jobs, and increase earnings for farmers and exporters. Kafeero confirmed Uganda's support for expanding African coffee trade under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), leveraging its 1.5 billion consumer market. Ethiopia, which produces 39% of Africa's coffee, and Uganda, with 23%, are central to this plan.

ug.headline: Uganda and EU target €2.2bn for green jobs
ug.dek: Trade between Uganda and the European Union has surged to €1.8 billion by 2025, with EU investments reaching €2.2 billion.
paragraphs: Uganda and the European Union are shifting focus to private capital, green manufacturing, and job creation, marking 50 years of diplomatic ties. The Uganda–European Union Business Forum in Kampala on October 20-21, 2026, alongside the Renewable Energy Conference and Expo, highlighted this new direction. Trade between Uganda and the bloc increased from roughly €420 million in 2015 to €1.8 billion by 2025.

European investments represented about 79 per cent of Uganda’s foreign direct investment inflows last year, totalling approximately €2.2 billion. Ambassador Jan Sadek stated the partnership uses Europe’s “Team Europe” and Global Gateway strategy to mobilize funding for sustainable projects. An upcoming €170-million overhaul of hydropower stations is backed by EU grants and development loans.

The Private Sector Foundation Uganda stressed that electricity must be reliable and affordable for manufacturers to benefit from expanded generation capacity. Minister of Energy Monica Musenero urged European investors to view renewable energy as a catalyst for industrial growth. Organizers will monitor if business matchmaking sessions yield financed projects translating into affordable power and employment.

cv.headline: Cabo Verde ranks third in governance index
cv.dek: The archipelago scores below its 2016 levels despite strong performance in rights and participation.
paragraphs: Cabo Verde ranks third in the Ibrahim Index of African Governance, behind Seychelles and Mauritius, but ahead of Botswana and South Africa. The 2026 IIAG report, covering 2016-2025, notes that the archipelago's overall score has declined from a decade ago, with deterioration accelerating in the last five years.

The country leads in the Rights category and performs well in Rule of Law and Justice, and Participation, contrasting with a continental trend where nearly 80% of Africans live in countries with declining rights. Cabo Verde also scores well on Women's Equality, yet it is among states where Security and Rule of Law, and Economic Opportunity foundations have worsened over the past decade.
The biennial index, published by the Ibrahim Foundation, uses 96 governance indicators. The official presentation of the 2026 IIAG findings is scheduled for today in Cairo.

cv.headline: Praia mayor seeks special status for capital city
cv.dek: Fernando Pinto argues the capital needs differentiated treatment due to its national responsibilities.
paragraphs: Fernando Pinto, mayor of Praia, is calling for the capital city to receive "differentiated treatment" to reflect its status as the nation's capital. He stated that Praia should be seen and treated as the capital, not just as a municipality, and actively participate in national solutions.

Pinto believes investment should be spread across all municipalities to prevent over-concentration of people and services in Praia. He highlighted that Praia receives a large influx from rural exodus, African coastal migration, cruise ships, and hosts the presidency, government, major companies, universities, and embassies, necessitating balanced national investment.

The mayor also emphasized the urgent need to invest in inter-island connectivity, allowing citizens to travel and work safely between islands like Praia and Maio. This initiative coincides with World Cities Day and aims to foster dialogue on urban development challenges in Cape Verde.

td.headline: Chad health ministry reports 14 dengue deaths amid rising fatalities
td.dek: Official figures from October 26 state 14 dengue deaths, while one mosque held 26 funerals on October 30.
paragraphs: Chad's Ministry of Public Health reported 14 deaths from dengue fever as of October 26, a figure sharply contrasted by local observations. Cemeteries in N'Djamena are reportedly full, and on October 30, the Markaz mosque alone conducted funeral prayers for 26 deceased individuals.

Hospitals, including the National Reference Hospital and private clinics, are overwhelmed, with patients reportedly being asked to lie on the floor. Families are seeking treatment while the government remains silent on the escalating crisis, offering no public response or appeal for international aid.

While provinces face intercommunal conflicts over resources, the health crisis is seen by some as a way for these issues to resolve themselves. Meanwhile, government officials met at the Radisson Blu hotel to discuss their actions, seemingly detached from the reality on the ground.

td.headline: Chad land dispute halts N'Djamena health center construction
td.dek: An association reports construction continues on land designated for a public health center in N'Djamena's Walia neighborhood.
paragraphs: The Association Action for the Well-being and Community Development in Chad (ABEDEC-TCHAD) has raised concerns about a land dispute in N'Djamena's Walia neighborhood that has lasted over eight years. The group denounces irregular land allocations and ongoing construction on a site reserved for a public health center. ABEDEC-TCHAD highlighted the situation on October 31, 2026, stating that a commission's 2018 report was irregularly established.

ABEDEC-TCHAD accuses Gaukam Claude, head of restructuring, and Hassana Hamit Mahamat, former deputy mayor, of irregularities in land distribution. The association claims a sharing of spaces on February 27, 2017, violated a 2008 decree on land allocation commissions. They also question how some beneficiaries obtained land documents and note that legal appeals by affected owners have been unsuccessful.

The dispute centers on land provided by a private individual for the Ngonba public health center, established administratively on September 20, 2016. The center currently operates in rented premises due to lack of site access. ABEDEC-TCHAD alleges Bolguel Lame Emmanuel is proceeding with construction despite a suspension order from June 3, 2025, confirmed on October 22, 2025. Work resumed on October 27, 2026, on the health reserve land.

The Assoungha seat has become vacant for the second time in the current legislative term. The ANGE has taken all necessary steps to ensure a transparent, credible, and fair election. Bartchiret also called on Assoungha voters to participate and for media professionals to provide balanced coverage.

dj.headline: Djibouti advocates for inclusive African digital future
dj.dek: Djibouti called for a continental digital ecosystem that is inclusive, sovereign, and innovative at a Libreville meeting.
paragraphs: Djibouti defended an "inclusive, sovereign, innovative" African digital future at a ministerial meeting in Libreville, Gabon. The gathering, which opened on Thursday, brought African states together to discuss digital transformation, communication infrastructure, and the governance of emerging technologies.

The meeting, held at the Palais des Congrès, aimed to strengthen cooperation among member states as digital transformation becomes a lever for growth and modernization. Participants reviewed the implementation of decisions from the November 2023 session in Addis Ababa and defined next steps, including electing a new bureau for the STC-CICT.

The STC-CICT, an AU technical body, harmonizes the continent's digital policies and guides decisions for the pan-African organization. The Libreville works concluded on Friday, with Djibouti reaffirming its commitment to enhancing African cooperation and building a digital ecosystem focused on the future.

sz.headline: Eswatini fuel prices surge 51.2% since April
sz.dek: The Ministry of Economic Planning and Development warns of increased production costs and weakened export competitiveness.
paragraphs: Fuel prices in Eswatini have risen by 51.2 per cent since April 2026, placing significant cost pressures on the economy. This increase threatens business competitiveness, reduces household purchasing power, and hinders economic recovery efforts.

The Ministry of Economic Planning and Development stated in its FY2026/27 Second Quarter Performance Report that persistent fuel price hikes, driven by Middle East tensions and global supply chain disruptions, have raised production costs. This situation significantly weakens Eswatini's export competitiveness and fuels inflation, which is currently limiting consumer spending.

Despite these challenges, Eswatini's economy grew by 6.5 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The primary sector expanded by 9.3 per cent, driven by agriculture and mining, while the industrial sector grew by 11.6 per cent, with manufacturing output up 14 per cent.

paragraphs: Mbabane Highlanders and Mbabane Swallows face off this afternoon in the Premier League of Eswatini (PLE) Charity Cup. This derby comes exactly 60 days after Highlanders defeated Swallows 4-0 in the 8Bet Trade Fair Cup quarter-finals.

sz.headline: Eswatini government seeks E3.79 billion in loans
sz.dek: The Ministry of Finance tabled three loan bills in the House of Assembly to finance development projects.
paragraphs: The Eswatini government is seeking E3.79 billion through loans to fund infrastructure and social development projects. Minister for Finance Neal Rijkenberg presented three loan Bills to the House of Assembly on Thursday.

One Bill seeks to authorise a loan of up to E1.6 billion from Standard Bank of South Africa Limited and other lenders. This borrowing is for projects agreed upon between the government and the arranger. The total public debt stood at E43.04 billion as of September 29, 2026.

The proposed loan will incur interest at a margin of 4.95 per cent per annum, plus arranging fees and facility management charges. An arranging fee could amount to E20.8 million based on the maximum facility. An annual management fee of E380,000 is also stipulated.

ga.headline: Gabon health ministry warns of late stroke treatment
ga.dek: Nearly 80% of stroke patients arrive at hospitals after the window for life-saving thrombolysis treatment has closed.
paragraphs: In Gabon, almost 80% of stroke patients reach hospitals too late for effective treatment, according to the Ministry of Health. This delay means victims often miss the critical window for thrombolysis, a procedure that can limit disability and save lives. The Centre hospitalier universitaire de Libreville (CHUL) saw its stroke admission rate rise from 42% in 2004 to 62.5% in 2025.

Minister of Health, Pr Elsa Nkana Joséphine Ayo épouse Bivigou, urged the public to recognize stroke symptoms and call for immediate help. A dedicated neurovascular unit at CHUL, established in 2021, has performed about 20 thrombolysis interventions. Hospital mortality for stroke patients has decreased from 9.5% in 2005 to 3.9% in 2026, but access to treatment remains limited by cost, as it is not covered by CNAMGS.

The ministry is advocating for more equitable access to stroke treatments and improved care throughout the entire chain, from initial alert to rehabilitation. Key risk factors include high blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, inactivity, overweight, and excessive alcohol consumption. The campaign's slogan emphasizes recognizing signs, alerting emergency services, and acting without delay.

ga.headline: Gabon civil society demands land deal explanation
ga.dek: 11 groups want parliament to question ministers over a plot given to the ruling party.
paragraphs: A coalition of Gabonese civil society groups has asked the National Assembly to question government officials about land allocated to the ruling party. The Union for Democracy and Builders (UDB) received a plot in Libreville's Plaine-Orety area. This site was previously declared for public utility, and residents were displaced in 2025.

The groups are demanding answers from Vice-President Hermann Immongault and Habitat Minister Mays Mouissi regarding the land's allocation. They seek clarity on the legal basis, size, and value of the land, as well as the decision-maker's identity. The UDB stated on October 24, 2026, that the land was acquired from competent authorities, but this has not resolved concerns.

The coalition also questions potential site reclassification and conflicts of interest, as the UDB's secretary-general holds a government position in the housing sector. They requested documentation of procedures and information on other beneficiaries. The groups also asked for a temporary halt to construction if necessary and clarification for displaced populations.

ga.headline: Gabon minister asks BEAC to ease property loan rules
ga.dek: Housing Minister Mays Mouissi met BEAC Governor Yvon Sana Bangui to discuss high interest rates and access to credit.
paragraphs: Gabon's Housing Minister Mays Mouissi met with the governor of the Bank of Central African States (BEAC), Yvon Sana Bangui, in Libreville on October 30, 2026. They discussed ways to make it easier for Gabonese households to get loans for buying property. The minister specifically raised concerns about the high interest rates charged by banks and difficulties in accessing financial information for loan applicants.

Governor Yvon Sana Bangui explained how the structure of bank deposits influences interest rates and the cost of credit in the region. The two officials agreed on the need to further explore options for making property loans more accessible. They considered measures to better regulate interest rates, which could improve borrowing conditions for families.

This meeting, held during the Open House for Housing event in Libreville from October 29 to 31, 2026, aims to support housing development by addressing financial barriers. The ministry is working with financial sector players to find solutions tailored to household budgets and facilitate property ownership.

ga.headline: Gabon health minister inspects Mouila health facilities
ga.dek: Minister Elsa Nkana Bivigou reviewed services from regional health direction to a provincial training school.
paragraphs: Gabon's Health Minister Elsa Nkana Bivigou inspected health facilities in Mouila on October 29, 2026. The minister visited the Regional Health Direction, the Ambulatory Treatment Centre, the urban health centre, maternal and child health services, the epidemiological base, and the provincial school for health workers. Her goal was to assess operations, identify issues, and improve care for the population.

During her tour, Minister Bivigou examined how services function, staff working conditions, and facility capacities. Discussions with managers revealed several shortcomings, leading to recommendations and requests for further explanation on operational reports. Working sessions are planned to determine corrective measures.

The minister also focused on the presence of specialist doctors redeployed to regional hospitals, a policy aimed at bringing specialized care closer to rural populations. Initial observations suggest this initiative is encouraging, with facilities seeing significant patient numbers seeking medical expertise now available in the provinces.

gm.headline: Gambia signs $169 million solar park deal
gm.dek: The agreement with Solaris Africa Ltd adds 148.44 MWp solar PV and 85 MW battery storage.
paragraphs: The Gambian government signed agreements today with Solaris Africa Ltd for Phase 2 of the Soma Solar Park, a deal valued at US$169 million. The project includes 148.44 MWp of solar PV and 85 MW of battery storage. The National Water and Electricity Company (NAWEC) signed a 25-year Power Purchase Agreement for the expansion.

The Ministry of Petroleum, Energy and Mines and the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs executed the Implementation Agreement. This project represents one of the largest private investments in The Gambia's energy sector. The battery storage component will enable solar power to supply the grid during evening peak demand.

This expansion aims to reduce reliance on expensive fuel-based electricity generation and improve the reliability of power for homes and businesses. The signing signals investor confidence in The Gambia as an open market and fulfills a commitment to provide reliable, affordable, and clean electricity to all citizens.

gm.headline: Gambia drug agency arrests 51 suspects in nationwide sweep
gm.dek: The Drug Law Enforcement Agency seized cannabis, cocaine, ecstasy, and crystal meth in operations across five regions.
paragraphs: The Drug Law Enforcement Agency, The Gambia (DLEAG) arrested 51 suspected drug offenders nationwide between October 14 and October 28, 2026. Operations seized cannabis, kush, cocaine, crack cocaine, ecstasy, and crystal meth. The suspects include 48 Gambians and three Senegalese nationals, with one alleged child offender aged 16 among them.

DLEAG Public Relations Officer Dawda Sanyang stated that 30 suspects were apprehended in the West Coast Region, 12 in Kanifing Municipality, five in North Bank Region, three in Banjul, and one in Central River Region. Notable arrests include Alagie Njie and Yasaye Ndure found with five parcels of skunk, and Kebba Mbye apprehended with two stones and three pieces of crack cocaine.

The agency also reported the seizure of 49 ecstasy pills from Yaya Kebbeh and six pieces of crack cocaine and two bags of ecstasy from Antouman Gaye. Saikou Sanyang was arrested with 51 parcels of cannabis and 81 pieces of kush, while Ousman Saidy and Ismaila Darboe were found with 93 wraps of cannabis and 85 pieces of kush. All 51 suspects remain in custody as investigations continue.

gm.headline: Russia and Africa forge equal partnership
gm.dek: The two continents are building cooperation on concrete projects aligned with African national priorities.
paragraphs: Russia and African nations are strengthening a partnership based on mutual respect and concrete projects, moving beyond empty promises. This approach aligns with the principle of "African solutions to African problems" and focuses on tangible benefits in sectors like energy, food security, education, and local business development. The partnership is structured around priorities identified by the African states themselves.

The Russia–Africa Summits and Economic and Humanitarian Forums serve as the primary mechanism for this cooperation. The first summit in Sochi in 2019 established a dialogue on an equal footing, leading to agreements in security, science, culture, and the economy. The second summit in St. Petersburg in 2023 included delegations from 48 countries, confirming the partnership's focus on concrete needs and projects.

The current Third Summit and Economic and Humanitarian Forum in Moscow feature approximately 40 sessions. These discussions are developed in collaboration with African partners, aiming for practical results in areas critical to the continent's development, including energy and infrastructure.

gm.headline: Man jailed seven months for stabbing brother
gm.dek: Basiru Sumareh admitted attempted murder and was sentenced to prison and ordered to pay compensation.
paragraphs: Basiru Sumareh received a seven-month prison sentence for attempting to kill his brother by stabbing him. Magistrate A. Darboe at the Brikama Magistrates’ Court convicted Sumareh on Thursday, 29 October, after he pleaded guilty to the charge. The incident occurred on 17 October 2026 in Brikama, West Coast Region, when Sumareh stabbed Baboucarr Sumareh in the chest and back with a knife.

Sumareh appeared in court without legal representation, while DSP K. Kinteh prosecuted the case. The court admitted a medical certificate, photographs of the victim's injuries, and the alleged weapon as evidence. Sumareh acknowledged the prosecution's facts, which detailed the stabbing with malice aforethought.

In sentencing, Magistrate Darboe cited Sumareh's early guilty plea as a mitigating factor but stressed the seriousness of the offence. Sumareh was sentenced to seven months at Mile 2 Central Prison and ordered to pay D100,000 in compensation to his brother, with an additional year of imprisonment for non-payment. The sentences are to run concurrently.

paragraphs: The Green Rise Africa Fellowship, a program by Acumen and Masafa Foundation, is offering Gambian entrepreneurs in the climate and green economy new opportunities. The fellowship is a six-month hybrid program with virtual workshops and in-person sessions across West Africa, designed to build resilience and values-driven leadership. Acumen’s mission is to invest in entrepreneurs who build inclusive societies, with the program aiming to help leaders examine their values and make intentional decisions.

Graduates gain lifelong membership in Acumen's global network of over 2,000 fellows, with access to peer collaboration and potential funding through the Angels Green Rise Africa program, offering grants of $25,000 or $50,000. Gambian entrepreneurs like Beran Dondeh Gillen of The Hub Ltd and Mariam Sarge of Electric Energy Solution have described the fellowship as transformational, helping them validate integrity and amplify their business stories.

paragraphs: The Association des Professionnels de la Publicité en Guinée (APP) met on Saturday, October 30, 2026, in Conakry to unify and restructure the advertising sector. Members of the new executive bureau and industry actors gathered to end internal divisions and build a strong, influential corporation for economic development.

Adama Diané, the new APP president, stated that despite past disagreements, the association is now talking again and aims to become a force for proposals. He emphasized that shared goals of defending interests, strengthening solidarity, and promoting the advertising sector in Guinea are transforming individual ambitions into a shared vision.

Diané highlighted the strategic role of advertising in Guinea's socio-economic fabric, calling for the APP to become a major institutional partner. The association's mission includes defending members' interests, promoting professions, and improving the business environment, contributing to national development efforts.

gn.headline: Mouctar Bah feted for 30 years at RFI, 38 at AFP
gn.dek: A surprise party in Conakry celebrated the veteran journalist's long career with Radio France internationale and Agence France-Presse.
paragraphs: Veteran journalist Mouctar Bah was surprised on Friday, October 30, 2026, in Conakry with a celebration marking his 30 years with Radio France internationale (RFI) and 38 years with Agence France-Presse (AFP). Dr. Safiatou Diallo orchestrated the event at the Centre international de recherche et documentation (CIRD), initially deceiving Bah into believing he was helping plan a party for her husband.

Bah arrived at the CIRD unaware he was the guest of honor, only to find family, friends, colleagues, and collaborators gathered. Video testimonials and speeches praised his experience, humility, helpfulness, and humor. Dr. Diallo, the event's initiator, expressed her delight at Bah's surprise and the heartfelt tributes.

Overwhelmed, Bah shared his emotion and gratitude, recalling significant events in Guinea he covered, including elections since 1998, rebel attacks on borders, and political demonstrations for freedom of expression and democracy. He described the tributes as touching and a profound reflection on his career.

Dr. Safiatou Diallo orchestrated the event at the Centre international de recherche et documentation (CIRD), initially deceiving Bah into believing he was helping plan a party for her husband.

Bah arrived at the CIRD unaware he was the guest of honor, only to find family, friends, colleagues, and collaborators gathered. Video testimonials and speeches praised his experience, humility, helpfulness, and humor. Dr. Diallo, the event's initiator, expressed her delight at Bah's surprise and the heartfelt tributes.

Overwhelmed, Bah shared his emotion and gratitude, recalling significant events in Guinea he covered, including elections since 1998, rebel attacks on borders, and political demonstrations for freedom of expression and democracy. He described the tributes as touching and a profound reflection on his career.

gn.headline: Yimbaya alumni clean up former school
gn.dek: Former students of Yimbaya High School organized a cleanup day to improve learning conditions and hygiene.
paragraphs: Alumni of Yimbaya High School in Conakry held a cleanup day on Saturday, October 31, 2026, to improve their former school. The Amicale des anciens élèves du lycée Yimbaya, with the school's administration and parent association, led the effort to clean, weed, and promote hygiene. This initiative is part of the alumni association's annual action plan to enhance the learning environment.

Mohamed Kaba, president of the alumni association, stated the cleanup was an act of gratitude and essential for learning. Activities included cleaning courtyards, classrooms, and school surroundings, maintaining water points, and installing waste bins. The day also featured hygiene awareness sessions for students. Other alumni groups, like Amicale Kötö Barry, joined the effort, emphasizing their shared connection to Yimbaya High School.

School principal Sékouba Oularé praised the alumni's commitment, calling it a concrete act of solidarity and responsibility. Matoto's deputy mayor, Aïssatou Barry, officially launched the event, encouraging students to maintain cleanliness daily. The initiative aims to foster a cleaner and healthier environment conducive to academic success.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau health ministry seeks national consultants
gw.dek: The Ministry of Public Health is recruiting two national consultants to bolster its PNDS Management Unit.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau's Ministry of Public Health is hiring two national consultants to strengthen its PNDS Management Unit (CG-PNDS). This unit manages a 27,535,509 Euro grant for fighting HIV/AIDS, TB, and reinforcing the health system, allocated for the 202-2026 period. The consultants will support technical and financial management of grant GC#8, and enhance the unit's programmatic and health system reinforcement efforts.

Applications must be submitted in a sealed envelope to the Secretary of the CG-PNDS by November 26, 2026, around 12:00. The required documents include a dated recommendation letter from the last employer, an updated curriculum vitae with three references, authenticated copies of diplomas and certificates, and a copy of an identity card or passport. These applications are addressed to the Director-General of Health System Administration.
This recruitment aims to enhance the capacity of the CG-PNDS to manage the allocated funding effectively.

gw.headline: Prime Minister demands swift Vigário Balanta death probe
gw.dek: Ilídio Vieira Té expresses concern over the slow progress in the investigation into the activist's March death.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau Prime Minister Ilídio Vieira Té publicly addressed the case of activist Vigário Luís Balanta, found dead in March near Nhacra, Oio region. Speaking on Friday, October 30, 2026, after meeting the Prosecutor-General and the President of the Court of Accounts, Té voiced his concern about the investigation's delay and his interest in its progress.

Vigário Luís Balanta, 35, was discovered deceased on March 31, 2026, in Ndam Lero, approximately 30 kilometers from Bissau, with visible signs of violence including stab wounds and gunshot injuries. The Prime Minister emphasized the need for the investigation to proceed to uncover the truth and deliver justice, thereby easing the victim's family's suffering.

The Prime Minister acknowledged the judicial institutions' challenges, citing insufficient human and material resources, and pledged the transitional government's support to the Prosecutor-General's and Court of Accounts' new teams. He also highlighted these institutions' strategic role in upholding legality and managing public finances, promising to address their limitations within the government's capacity.

lr.headline: Swiss court upholds Kosiah's 20-year war crimes sentence
lr.dek: Former ULIMO commander Alieu Kosiah will serve 20 years for atrocities in Lofa County during Liberia's civil war.
paragraphs: Switzerland's Federal Supreme Court has confirmed a 20-year prison sentence for former ULIMO commander Alieu Kosiah for war crimes committed in Liberia's Lofa County between 1993 and 1995. The ruling upholds the conviction for acts including killing civilians, rape, and using child soldiers, making it the first war crimes conviction by a Swiss civilian court and the first for a Liberian national for civil war atrocities.

The court acquitted Kosiah of crimes against humanity, a charge added by an appeals chamber in 2023, stating the relevant Swiss law was not in effect at the time of the crimes. This acquittal does not alter his 20-year sentence, the maximum allowed under Swiss law, nor his eventual expulsion from Switzerland. Alain Werner of Civitas Maxima, representing victims, welcomed the final conviction but expressed disappointment over the acquittal.

Kosiah, who settled in Switzerland in the late 1990s, has been detained since his arrest in November 2014 following a complaint by Liberian victims. Survivors traveled from Liberia to testify against him during the investigation and trials. The case was supported by the Liberian organization Global Justice and Research Project (GJRP), which has helped secure five convictions in six trials linked to Liberia's civil wars.

lr.headline: Whein Town residents demand landfill closure
lr.dek: Residents near Monrovia's Whein Town Landfill face swarms of flies, rodents, and foul smells, fearing health risks.
paragraphs: Residents of Whein Town, near Monrovia, are enduring unbearable conditions due to the continued operation of the Whein Town Landfill. Swarms of flies, foul-smelling water, and the presence of rodents and snakes have made daily life difficult, with residents reporting increased costs for clean water and protection for their children.

Amos Moore, a resident, stated that the government has failed to honor its commitment to close the landfill after its original five-year lifespan expired, calling the situation a "shame" that inflicts suffering. Samuel Kofi Jones III, Secretary General of the Whein Town Community Leadership, confirmed years of complaints and protests against harmful activities at the facility.

Public health and environmental experts warn that poorly managed landfills exceeding their capacity pose serious risks to nearby populations. The Monrovia City Corporation acknowledges the landfill has outlived its usefulness and claims to be taking "immediate, aggressive action," but residents say dumping has not ended.

lr.headline: Liberia group slams Boakai-Koung over poverty, pay gaps
lr.dek: STAND demands probe into president's son amid claims of US$14,000 salaries for some officials.
paragraphs: The Solidarity & Trust for a New Day (STAND) has accused the Boakai-Koung administration of failing ordinary Liberians and allowing wide salary disparities within government. STAND stated that the government’s billion-dollar budget has not translated into meaningful relief for citizens struggling with poverty, poor public services, and economic hardship. The group also questioned why senior Central Bank of Liberia (CBL) officials reportedly receive substantial salaries and allowances while some lower-paid public workers face salary reductions.

STAND Chairman Mulbah K. Morlu Jr. said the government’s approach to public spending and accountability reflects a growing gap between senior officials' privileges and ordinary citizens' difficulties. The group cited reported monthly salaries of US$14,000 and US$15,000 in housing allowances for some senior CBL officials, contrasting this with a Governance Commission employee facing a pay cut from US$1,281.91 to US$900. STAND called on government bodies to explain the disparities and subject public-sector compensation to an independent review.

Beyond economic concerns, STAND reiterated its call for an independent investigation into drug trafficking allegations involving Joseph Boakai Jr., arguing that political and family connections should not influence legal application. The group demanded that any unlawful or improperly authorized decisions be corrected and responsible parties held accountable.

lr.headline: Liberia enrolls 409 volunteer teachers on payroll
lr.dek: Monrovia Consolidated School System classes resume after government commits to address salary and welfare issues.
paragraphs: Academic activities have resumed at the Monrovia Consolidated School System (MCSS) after the Liberian government committed to resolving teachers' grievances. The government enrolled an additional 201 volunteer teachers, bringing the total formally enrolled to 409. Outstanding salaries are also being disbursed as part of the resolution.

MCSS Superintendent Dr. Augurie E. Stevens announced the resumption on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, thanking stakeholders for constructive dialogue. She stated that the enrollment addresses the plight of educators who served without full employment benefits. The decision follows recent protests by teachers and students over unresolved issues.

The government's commitment, supported by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai's administration, aims to find permanent solutions for public school teachers. Education advocates stress the need for sustained attention to prevent future disruptions. The priority for students and families remains uninterrupted learning and a stable education system.

lr.headline: Liberia receives 30 road machines for farming
lr.dek: Bong County's new heavy equipment aims to improve market access for farmers and rural families.
paragraphs: 30 heavy earthmoving machines have arrived in Bong County, Liberia, to improve rural infrastructure. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Executive Director Dr. Emmanuel King Urey Yarkpawolo stated that these machines are intended for construction work that could connect farmers to markets and improve the lives of rural families.

Dr. Yarkpawolo, a native of Zota District, emphasized that passable roads are essential for food security and farm income, directly impacting rural households. He commended President Joseph Nyuma Boakai for placing roads at the center of his administration’s agenda, which he believes will alleviate transportation issues hindering agriculture and trade in Bong County.

The EPA chief explained that poor roads cause harvested crops like rice and cassava to spoil before reaching markets, leading to farmer losses. He added that improved roads can help children reach school and patients reach hospitals, and enable businesses to reach new customers.

ly.headline: UN extends Libya mission until October 2027
ly.dek: Security Council resolution backs efforts to unify state institutions and hold elections within two years.
paragraphs: The United Nations Security Council has extended its political mission in Libya until October 31, 2027. The resolution supports efforts to unify state institutions and establish a single executive authority. It also urges Libyan parties to commit to holding national elections within 24 months.

Resolution 2835, adopted on Friday, October 30, renews support for Hanna Tetteh, the UN secretary-general’s special representative. Britain led negotiations on the text, which supports the “4+4” process agreement reached on August 30. This agreement provides for changes to the electoral framework and leadership of the High National Elections Commission.

The Council calls for a broader UN presence across Libya, including in Benghazi, Sabha, and Sirte, with greater engagement in the east and south. A dedicated economic section will address fuel smuggling, diversion of public funds, and illicit exploitation of state resources, stressing that petroleum resources belong to all Libyans.

ly.headline: Libya and Italy sign economic cooperation deal
ly.dek: Tripoli Chamber of Commerce and the Joint Italian-Arab Chamber of Commerce agreed to boost trade and investment.
paragraphs: The Tripoli Chamber of Commerce signed a memorandum of understanding with the Joint Italian-Arab Chamber of Commerce on October 29 in Milan, Italy. The agreement aims to strengthen economic and commercial cooperation between Libya and Italy. Anwar Abu Sitta, Chairman of the Tripoli Chamber, and Pietro Rompino, President of the JIACC, signed the deal.

The memorandum seeks to foster private sector economic relations, encourage joint ventures, and facilitate communication between Libyan and Italian companies. Cooperation will cover sectors including energy, infrastructure, agriculture, pharmaceuticals, and digital services. The agreement also focuses on developing young entrepreneurs through training and expertise exchange.

Future cooperation includes organizing a Libyan-Italian Business Forum alternately in each country, facilitating business-to-business and business-to-government meetings, and encouraging participation in trade exhibitions. This initiative was part of the 5th Arab-Italian Economic Forum.

ly.headline: Libyan PM discusses market instability with traders
ly.dek: Abdel Hamid Aldabaiba met with traders and chambers of commerce in Misrata to address commodity prices and import regulations.
paragraphs: Libyan Prime Minister Abdel Hamid Aldabaiba met with traders and representatives from chambers of commerce and industry today in the Misrata Free Zone. The meeting focused on rising commodity prices, mechanisms for opening documentary credits, the market dollar exchange rate, and the customs dollar.

Discussions also covered the Minister of Economy and Trade's decision to limit import operations to banking channels and an evaluation of economic decisions regulating imports. Aldabaiba stressed the need for balanced measures to ensure goods availability, control price increases, and maintain citizens' purchasing power.

The meeting was attended by several ministers, including the Minister of Economy and Trade, Suhail Abu Shiha, and the Minister of Transport, Mohamed Al-Shahoubi. Aldabaiba called for enhanced coordination between government agencies and the private sector to address market imbalances.

ly.headline: Libya limits insulin distribution to electronic system
ly.dek: New insulin shipments have arrived, but distribution will now only reach registered patients.
paragraphs: Libya's National Diabetes Authority will now only distribute insulin to patients registered in its electronic system. Awad Al-Quweri, the authority's head, announced this change, stating that insulin will not be dispensed outside this organized framework. Al-Quweri confirmed that three new shipments of insulin have arrived in the country.

Al-Quweri explained the new distribution policy to Al-Massar TV, emphasizing the move towards an electronic system for dispensing the vital medication. This measure aims to streamline access for those already enrolled in the digital registry. The arrival of three new batches offers a supply update for the nation's diabetic population.

The authority's announcement means that individuals not yet registered in the electronic system will face challenges in obtaining insulin. The specific quantity of insulin in the new shipments was not detailed. Further updates on the electronic system's capacity and registration process are expected.

ly.headline: Armed group closes Libya oil pipeline valve
ly.dek: National Oil Corporation reports 15,000 barrels per day of crude oil supply to Zawia refinery disrupted.
paragraphs: An armed group closed a valve on the main Al-Hamada crude oil pipeline in the Al-Rayayna area today, disrupting supplies to the Zawia refinery.

The National Oil Corporation (NOC) stated that the forced closure of the 18-inch diameter pipeline caused a pressure spike, halting pumping operations by 12:30 AM last night to protect infrastructure.

mg.headline: Madagascar university officials detained over fake diplomas
mg.dek: Three senior staff at Itasy University in Soavinandriana face pre-trial detention for alleged diploma fraud.
paragraphs: Three senior officials at Itasy University in Soavinandriana, Madagascar, have been placed in pre-trial detention following an investigation into fake diplomas. Two other individuals are under judicial supervision. The case, initiated by the Independent Anti-Corruption Bureau (Bianco), centers on the alleged use of falsified degrees to secure positions within the university.

The implicated officials include the former university president, the director of the Higher School of Engineering, and an administrative and financial manager. Investigations revealed a system of issuing and using fake Bachelor's and Master's 2 degrees from Itasy University, reportedly to justify administrative appointments. The charges include fabrication and use of false documents, abuse of function, and illicit gains.

The Public Prosecutor's Office stated that investigations are ongoing, with potential for further examination of irregularities and responsibilities. The case involves alleged offenses such as forgery, abuse of office, and complicity in obtaining undue advantages.

mg.headline: Madagascar president attends Russia-Africa summit

paragraphs: The president of the Republic Refoundation of Madagascar (PRRM) attended the third Russia-Africa summit in Moscow on October 29, 2026, meeting with Vladimir Putin. The summit saw 48 African delegations, 22 led by heads of state, a rise from 17 in 2023.

Analysts debated whether Africa is becoming a 'Russafrique' after 'Françafrique,' questioning if the continent is at the table or on the menu. Russia's trade with Africa grew from $18 billion in 2022 to over $27 billion in 2025, falling short of its goal to double exchanges to $40 billion. Russian arms imports to Africa decreased from 24% in 2019-2023 to 15% in 2021-2025.

Madagascar's military cooperation with Russia, initiated in 2018 and updated in 2022, reportedly scaled up after an unspecified rupture in October 2025. The summit's final declaration and an action plan for 2027-2029 were adopted, alongside a separate, non-binding action plan between the African Union Commission and Russia.

mg.headline: Madagascar and Italy boost film heritage ties
mg.dek: Minister Gascar Fenosoa visited Bologna to discuss preserving and digitizing Malagasy cinema archives.
paragraphs: Madagascar is strengthening its cultural cooperation with Italy to safeguard, restore, and digitize its film and audiovisual heritage. Minister of Communication and Culture Gascar Fenosoa traveled to Bologna, Italy, to meet with the Fondazione Cineteca di Bologna and its laboratory, L’Immagine Ritrovata. The discussions focused on conserving archives, digitizing films, restoring old movies, upgrading equipment, and training Malagasy professionals.

The initiative aims to improve the preservation of audiovisual materials held at the Auditorium Andohibe, making them more accessible to the public. Minister Fenosoa stated that understanding history and protecting its documentation are essential for consolidating Malagasy identity and preparing the country's future. This vision links heritage preservation with education, creation, and cinema development.

The collaboration builds on existing economic and technical cooperation between Madagascar and Italy, established by an agreement on July 1, 1964. This new focus on audiovisual heritage seeks to deepen these bilateral relations. Officials from the Cineteca di Bologna, including Director Gian Luca Farinelli and Deputy Director Davide Pietrantoni, participated in the meetings.

mw.headline: Mutharika returns, blames fuel and power issues on saboteurs
mw.dek: President Peter Mutharika stated he was in full control of Malawi during his absence and promised consequences for electricity disruptions.
paragraphs: President Peter Mutharika returned to Malawi on Saturday after a private trip to South Africa and asserted he remained in charge of the country. He stated he was in constant contact with the Chief Secretary and ministers, dismissing speculation about other officials running the government in his absence. Mutharika also warned individuals deliberately causing problems in the electricity sector that they would face consequences.

The President attributed persistent electricity disruptions to man-made issues, promising that blackouts would end by December as machines were being repaired. Regarding fuel shortages, Mutharika explained that supplies were available at ports in Tanzania and Mozambique, including Nacala, Beira, Tanga, and Dar es Salaam, but logistics were hindering transportation into Malawi. He asked for patience, stating these fuel transportation challenges were beyond government control.

Mutharika, who has made five private trips since October 2025, thanked citizens for messages during his absence and called for unity using the Swahili expression 'Harambee'. He arrived home on Saturday, November 1, 2026, following his nearly month-long trip.

mw.headline: Malawi U-15 team finishes 79th at Fifa World Cup
mw.dek: The team's performance in Baku exposed significant gaps in the nation's youth football development structures.
paragraphs: Malawi's Under-15 boys national football team concluded the inaugural Fifa Under-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan, ranked 79th out of 189 nations. The team secured 15th place in Tier C after achieving five victories against Chinese Taipei, Oman, Suriname, Hungary, and Rwanda. Takutzwa Maluwe was Malawi's top scorer with eight goals, contributing to the team's overall performance.

Despite individual successes like Maluwe's eight goals, defeats against Algeria, Argentina, Luxembourg, Panama, and Thailand highlighted areas needing substantial improvement in Malawi's youth football development. Namasala Academy owner Wesley Namasala observed that international competitiveness requires sustained investment in coaching, facilities, nutrition, and competitive opportunities, noting that foreign players were often more physically developed.

Namasala proposed establishing at least 10 residential academies across Malawi to build a strong foundation, stating that short training camps cannot replace childhood development. Zambia's success in winning Tier B by assembling a squad from 11 schools also suggests schools football as a viable alternative pathway for talent development in Malawi.

mw.headline: Malawi parliament meeting postponed after presidential recommendation
mw.dek: President Mutharika recommended postponing the National Assembly's session, with the Speaker announcing the change.
paragraphs: Malawi's National Assembly meeting, scheduled from November 9 to December 11, 2026, has been postponed. President Peter Mutharika sent a letter on October 23, 2026, recommending the postponement to redirect public resources to national challenges. The Speaker subsequently announced the postponement of the Fourth Meeting of the 52nd Session.

The use of the word 'directed' in the President's letter has raised constitutional questions. Section 59 of the Constitution states that the Speaker, in consultation with the President, appoints the time for every meeting of the National Assembly. The President can also, in consultation with the Speaker, summon extraordinary meetings or prorogue the Assembly.

The Constitution does not expressly provide for postponement, but outlines the consultative relationship between the President and the Speaker regarding parliamentary sittings. The Speaker takes part in fixing when a meeting starts, and the President has an express power to prorogue, subject to consultation.

mw.headline: Malawi expands cancer treatment services

paragraphs: Malawi has increased access to specialised cancer care at the National Cancer Centre within Kamuzu Central Hospital (KCH) in Lilongwe. Patients can now receive surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy locally, reducing the need for expensive overseas treatment. Health officials noted progress in cancer services despite challenges like late diagnoses.

In 2025, KCH registered over 2,100 new cancer patients, with more than 1,600 receiving chemotherapy and over 600 undergoing radiotherapy. Amos Msekandiana, KCH Director General, stated that the centre also provided brachytherapy to 70 women. He highlighted the need for more oncologists, nurses, and technicians to improve care, noting that many patients still present with late-stage disease.

The Ministry of Health and Sanitation aims to strengthen cancer control through the National Cancer Control Strategic Plan 2019-2029. Benson Chisamile, Secretary for Health and Sanitation, mentioned progress in prevention, including HPV vaccination and screening, and training over 2,000 health workers in childhood cancer detection. Msekandiana also called for investment in psychosocial support for patients.

mw.headline: Malawi central bank raises borrowing costs
mw.dek: The Reserve Bank of Malawi increased its Lombard Rate to 2 percent to manage liquidity amid inflation risks.
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) has raised its Lombard Rate from 0.2 percentage points to 2 percentage points, increasing borrowing costs for businesses and consumers. This move by the Monetary Policy Committee aims to manage liquidity amidst inflation risks, with economist Velli Nyirongo warning of tough times ahead. Businesses relying on imported materials and fuel will face higher operational costs, potentially limiting expansion and new ventures.

Nyirongo stated that while the rate hike may help contain inflation risks, its direct impact will be limited because external factors like high fuel prices and imported costs also drive inflation. He emphasized the need for government coordination on food supply, agricultural production, and fiscal discipline to support the fight against rising prices. The current inflation rate dropped to 20.1 percent in the third quarter from 22.9 percent.

The RBM's Monetary Policy Committee noted that broad money growth slowed to 19.7 percent in the third quarter of 2026, down from 21.2 percent in the previous quarter and significantly lower than 51 percent a year earlier. Private sector credit growth also slowed to 21.7 percent. However, the use of the Lombard facility rose to an average of K72.3 billion per day, posing a risk to money supply growth.

ml.headline: Malians buy street drugs amid high pharmacy costs
ml.dek: Doctors warn of poisoning and treatment failure from unregulated medicines sold without prescriptions.
paragraphs: In Bamako and other Malian cities, people are buying medicines from street vendors, known as 'pharmacie par terre,' because pharmacy prices are too high. This practice exposes buyers to health risks like treatment failure and poisoning, according to health professionals.

General practitioner Harouna Doumbia stated that financial hardship, vendor proximity, and easy purchase without a prescription drive people to street drugs. Vendor Aly Keita confirmed that amoxicillin is a popular item, sold between 25F CFA and 500F CFA, often without proper refrigeration.

Dr. Doumbia warned that unknown drug compositions can cause poisoning and organ damage, while under-dosed products may lead to treatment failure and disease progression, delaying proper diagnosis and care.

His song "Oh My Baby" reached the Shazam charts in Ivory Coast in October.

Pakenzy works independently without a label, collaborating with beatmaker Wippa Beat and his team. He aims for accessible and danceable songs that reflect the realities of his generation, focusing on themes of youth, love, and betrayal. He emphasizes patience, perseverance, and consistency in building his career, stating that it requires time, passion, and a connection with people.

The artist carefully manages his image through elegant appearances, clips, and social media performances to establish a recognizable identity. He has collaborated with artists like Sadio Sidibé, Dr Keb, and MS2 on tracks such as "Diarabi" in July 2024 and "FAMA" in January 2025. Pakenzy believes his music can bring happiness, dreams, and life lessons.

mr.headline: Mauritania centre holds seminar on teacher training reform
mr.dek: The Educational Research and Studies Centre organised a seminar to discuss the reality and prospects of initial teacher training.
paragraphs: The Educational Research and Studies Centre, in cooperation with the National Federation of Parents' Associations and the Municipality of Toujounine, held a scientific seminar on Saturday evening. The event, titled “Reform of the Initial Training System in Teacher Training Schools: Reality and Prospects,” aimed to enhance discussion on the current state and future development of teacher training.

The seminar is part of the centre’s monthly programme, “Discussions on Education in Mauritania,” and was held to celebrate World Teachers' Day. Mr. Ba Hammady Hussein, the centre's vice president, stated that the seminar aimed to open public discussion on education issues in Mauritania, highlighting the importance of initial teacher training as a cornerstone for successful educational reform.

Lecturer Mohamed Elamine Ould Elban presented an overview of teacher training schools, focusing on the specificities of the teacher training school in Nouakchott. He discussed the challenges these institutions face and the opportunities available for their development and performance improvement.

mu.headline: Menlo Park demands $19.55 million from Bank of Mauritius
mu.dek: Company claims former central bank governor Rama Sithanen sought commission on financing deal before his appointment.
paragraphs: Menlo Park Ltd served a legal demand on the Bank of Mauritius on October 30, seeking $19.55 million in damages. The company claims $9.25 million for loss of share value, $5.3 million for lost investment, and $5 million for reputational damage. The bank has one month to comply or face legal action.

The demand alleges that Rama Sithanen, his son Tevin Sithanen, and Ziyad Bundhun discussed a financing request with Menlo Park between October 17 and 24, 2024. According to the claim, Rama Sithanen suggested he could unblock $6.3 million from the MIC if a commission was paid to him or his son. Menlo Park states it refused this arrangement.

After Rama Sithanen became governor on November 16, 2024, he publicly called the MIC investment a fraud on December 7, 2024, freezing Menlo Park's account. The company views this as retribution. A WhatsApp call recording from November 12, 2024, involving Tevin Sithanen, has also become public, with claims of his father's influence over the MIC and threats of arrest.

mu.headline: Mauritius cabinet considers lowering age of criminal responsibility
mu.dek: Government examines prosecuting 12-year-olds after recent riots, but legal experts and child rights groups raise concerns.
paragraphs: The Mauritian government is considering lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 12 years old, a move prompted by recent riots where minors were arrested. The current law, established by the Children’s Act 2020, sets the minimum age at 14. Cabinet discussed the proposal on October 14, but decided on further consultation and a parliamentary Select Committee before any decision is made.

Police reported that 16 out of 151 people arrested during the unrest were minors, approximately one in nine. However, legal experts point out that a retroactive change would not apply to these arrests due to constitutional protections. The proposed reform would only affect future cases, and concerns remain about the justice system's capacity to handle cases involving younger children, given existing delays highlighted in past Privy Council rulings.

Child-rights organisations and the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child advise against lowering the age, citing potential harm to children and a lack of evidence that prosecuting younger children deters violence. The current system, designed for those aged 14 and above, would require significant changes to accommodate 12- and 13-year-olds, including staff training and facility adjustments. The Select Committee will also examine parental responsibility and the role of adults inciting minors to commit crimes.

mu.headline: Mauritians honour ancestors with cemetery rituals
mu.dek: Families across the island spent November 1 and 2 cleaning and decorating graves for All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day.
paragraphs: Thousands of Mauritian families gathered at cemeteries across the island, including Saint-Jean in Quatre-Bornes and Salines in Port-Louis, on November 1 and 2. They cleaned, renovated, and decorated the graves of their departed loved ones for All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day.

Fabrice, a 45-year-old resident of Curepipe, explained his annual visit to his grandparents' graves at Saint-Jean cemetery. He stated, "I repaint their tombs, not just to update them and keep them clean, but it's a way to tell my grandparents: 'Yes… I love you and I haven't forgotten you.'" Families used water, brushes, paint, and flowers like lilies, carnations, and tropical bouquets to adorn the tombs.

Despite rising costs for imported and local flowers, most families are committed to maintaining this tradition. Fabrice added, "Whatever the cost of flowers, paint, or renovation… we do it out of love and respect for our elders." The annual observance highlights the strength of family ties and cultural continuity in Mauritius.

mz.headline: Mozambique renews Kenmare titanium mine concession until 2044
mz.dek: The Council of Ministers approved the extension for the Moma mine, which supplies 6% of global titanium feedstocks.
paragraphs: Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved the extension of rights and concessions for Kenmare Resources' Moma heavy mineral sands mine in Nampula province until 2044. The approval, granted on October 13 and officially notified on October 29, includes changes to the tax, commercial, and investment regimes.

The Moma mine, operated by Kenmare since 2007, accounts for approximately 6% of the world's titanium feedstocks, supplying industries such as paint and plastics in over 15 countries. Managing director Tom Hickey stated the changes aim for a balance between Kenmare's interests and a greater contribution to Mozambique.

Royalties on gross revenues will increase progressively from 1% to 5% by 2044. Kenmare Resources had been negotiating the renewal since its initial 20-year authorization expired in December 2024, having previously threatened international arbitration over fiscal terms.

mz.headline: Mozambique plans private rail operators
mz.dek: State-owned CFM will tender sections of the national rail network to attract more freight traffic.
paragraphs: Ports and Railways of Mozambique (CFM) is preparing tenders to allow private companies to operate parts of the national rail network. The state-owned company aims to attract more freight traffic and boost Mozambique's role as a transit hub for neighboring countries. CFM will remain the infrastructure manager while private firms operate services under concession.

Mozambique's freight network uses three corridors linked to the ports of Maputo, Beira, and Nacala. In the first quarter of 2026, railways carried 3.6 million metric tons of goods, a 14.9% increase year-on-year. The government announced a 14-billion-metical investment program for 2025–2030 to upgrade infrastructure, including new locomotives and freight cars.

The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique called for more reliable rail operations and reviewed freight rates in June 2026. Exporters sometimes favor road transport due to unpredictable delivery times and railcar shortages. The success of the concessions will depend on efficient coordination with ports, customs, and road transport.

mz.headline: Mozambique and China advance cassava value chain
mz.dek: A meeting in Shenzhen mapped implementation of a memorandum of understanding signed in Maputo to boost cultivation, processing, and commercialization.
paragraphs: Mozambique and China have entered a new phase of cassava value chain development following a meeting in Shenzhen between the Mozambique Chamber of Commerce (CCMI) and Chinese partners. This follows a Memorandum of Understanding signed in Maputo on October 1.

The initiative, attended by CCMI Board Chairperson Thani Cabir and Executive Director Fileu Pave, will initially target the Gaza and Inhambane provinces. Local cooperatives, business associations, and the Longrun Group will engage in cassava cultivation, processing, and commercialization, with Longrun Group facilitating technology transfer and employment.

China annually imports four million tonnes of cassava chips, eight million tonnes of starch, 1.5 million tonnes of unprocessed cassava, and over 50,000 tonnes of flour, presenting a significant export opportunity for Mozambique. This sustained demand aims to diversify agricultural exports, boost domestic value addition, and uplift rural smallholders and agro-industrial SMEs.

na.headline: Bank of Namibia grants farmers loan holidays
na.dek: Commercial banks must offer up to 24-month repayment breaks to farmers and businesses hit by disease and drought.
paragraphs: The Bank of Namibia directed commercial banks on Friday to provide loan repayment moratoriums of up to 24 months for farmers and businesses affected by Foot-and-Mouth Disease and anticipated El Niño conditions. Banking institutions must assess borrowers' financial circumstances and income losses before granting relief, which can range from one to 24 months. Banks may also restructure loans to make repayments more manageable, though interest will continue to accrue unless otherwise agreed in writing.

This intervention follows concerns raised by the agricultural and banking sectors about financially distressed farmers and businesses. Eligibility extends to companies within the agricultural value chain whose income depends on farming. Borrowers must demonstrate that their income has been adversely affected by the disease outbreak or climatic conditions. The central bank also introduced protections for credit bureau reporting, requiring banks to report clients receiving relief as performing.

The Bank of Namibia stated the measure aims to support the agricultural sector's viability, protect livelihoods, and limit financial system risks. Agriculture is a significant contributor to employment, food security, and economic growth. The FMD outbreak and adverse climatic conditions pose risks across the agricultural value chain. Banks must provide written reasons for declining applications, and borrowers can lodge complaints through internal processes.

na.headline: Namibians question prison comfort versus street struggle
na.dek: Life outside correctional facilities offers less security and fewer basic services than life inside, prompting serious discussion.
paragraphs: Namibians are debating whether life inside prison has become more comfortable than life on the streets, with citizens facing daily struggles for food, shelter, and employment. Street vendors have their goods confiscated, while inmates receive accommodation, meals, water, electricity, and healthcare.

The discussion highlights a disparity in the provision of basic needs and opportunities between those incarcerated and those living freely but in poverty. While prisoners are human beings deserving of dignity and rehabilitation, questions arise about the commitment to improving the lives of law-abiding citizens struggling to survive.

The core issue is creating a society outside prison that offers more meaningful opportunities and dignity than the security some inmates may find within. The argument is not for harsher prison conditions but for increased investment in crime prevention, job creation, and support for vulnerable communities to make life outside prison more viable.

na.headline: Woman found dead in Otjiwarongo flat
na.dek: Police investigate multiple stab wounds after ex-boyfriend dies in road incident.
paragraphs: Kamilla Rickerts, 34, was found dead with multiple stab wounds in her ex-boyfriend’s flat in Otjiwarongo on Sunday. Police confirmed that Jovin Diergaardt, her ex-boyfriend, allegedly picked her up on Saturday and took her to his flat. Diergaardt later died in a road incident near Swakopmund on Sunday morning.

Otjozondjupa police spokesperson senior inspector Maureen Mbeha stated that preliminary investigations suggest Kamilla was last seen with Diergaardt around midday on Saturday. Diergaardt reportedly travelled to Swakopmund and died about 15km from the town towards Arandis, with police indicating he may have jumped in front of a moving truck. Kamilla had recently moved to Otjiwarongo and had been there for a week before her death.

Heinrich Rickerts, Kamilla’s brother, described her as his best friend and confidante, noting she helped raise their niece and younger sister. Kamilla, who would have turned 35 on November 14, will be buried near Rehoboth next Saturday. Police investigations into the incident are ongoing, and they have cautioned against spreading unverified information.

na.headline: Bank of Namibia buys 425kg of gold
na.dek: The central bank's gold accumulation programme aims to boost financial resilience and diversify reserves.
paragraphs: The Bank of Namibia has purchased 425kg of gold from local mines as part of its gold accumulation programme, aiming for a total of 600kg. This initiative, started last year, seeks to strengthen the country's financial resilience and diversify its international reserves. Deputy governor Nicholas Mukasa stated that gold purchases have significantly contributed to the recent increase in international reserves.

Namibia's international reserves grew from N$58 billion to N$59.3 billion between the end of July and September. These reserves currently provide 3.6 months of import cover, which is adequate for currency peg support and international obligations. Gold offers an additional layer of protection against geopolitical tensions and volatile financial markets, unlike foreign currency assets.

Gold complements traditional reserve assets because its value does not always move with other holdings, promoting prudent reserve management. South Africa and Ghana also hold gold as a reserve asset, with Ghana pursuing a domestic gold purchasing strategy. China and Poland have also expanded their gold holdings for protection against external shocks.

na.headline: Namibia loses N$67.8bn to illicit financial flows
na.dek: The finance minister expressed deep concern over suspected money laundering and tax evasion impacting public services.
paragraphs: Namibia potentially lost N$67.8 billion to illicit financial flows over three years, averaging N$22.6 billion annually, according to the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC). Finance Minister Ericah Shafudah stated these unlawful activities, including tax evasion and money laundering, undermine domestic revenue and economic development.

Shafudah highlighted that such diversions deprive the country of resources needed for public services and infrastructure. She warned that professional confidentiality should not shield financial crimes, urging accountants and auditors to report suspicious transactions and cooperate with authorities.

Legislative reforms are underway to improve public finance management, including the proposed Public Finance Management Bill. The government also aims to strengthen the Auditor-General's office and modernise the regulation of the accounting profession.

ne.headline: Niger forces neutralise seven mercenaries
ne.dek: Military operations in October recovered weapons, communication devices, and destroyed armed group bases.
paragraphs: Nigerien security forces neutralised seven mercenaries during operations across the country in the second half of October 2026. The Centre Intégré de Coordination des Operations (CICO) reported that Operation Damissa, near the Nigerian border, saw ground forces destroy enemy bases and shelters.

In the north, two armed bandits were killed near Amazguèr on October 20 after firing on a patrol, with two rifles and ammunition seized. Two days later, in Tabarkat, four AK-47 rifles, two M80 machine guns, and hundreds of communication devices were confiscated. West of the country, one mercenary was neutralised in Tinfagatt, and a logistical base was destroyed.

The CICO report also detailed the October 16 neutralisation of a Boko Haram fighter near N’Guigmi, with one suspect arrested for supplying the group. On October 24, former Boko Haram fighters surrendered in Bosso with their families, handing over two AK-47 rifles and ammunition.

This delivery clarifies the presence of Algerian soldiers in Niger, who were seen escorting the fuel trucks. The official reception of this first shipment is scheduled for Sunday, November 1, in Agadez, with the Nigerien Minister of Petroleum expected to attend.

The initiative continues the cooperation between Algeria and Niger, particularly in the Agadez region. This partnership has historically included health, education, trade, and infrastructure projects, with Algeria also contributing to the Trans-Saharan road and fiber optic projects.

ne.headline: Niger journalist Moussa Kaka detained for two months
ne.dek: Moussa Kaka, a journalist for radio television Saraounia, has been held incommunicado since August 31.
paragraphs: Journalist Moussa Kaka has been detained in Niger for two months without seeing his family or lawyer. Kaka left his media outlet in Niamey on August 31 and never arrived home. The Nigerien Minister of Justice Alio Daouda confirmed Kaka was alive and detained in early October, according to Reporters Without Borders (RSF).

Sadibou Marong, RSF's director for sub-Saharan Africa, stated that the organization is demanding information and calling for Kaka's immediate release. RSF believes Niger is violating its international commitments by holding the journalist in secret. Kaka was known for reporting on Nigerien news for RFI Afrique.

RSF is calling for Kaka's release and for Niger to uphold its international obligations. The organization has not received further information on Kaka's whereabouts or legal status since the minister's statement.

paragraphs: INES-Ruhengeri graduated 1,729 students on Thursday, October 30, in Musanze district. The graduates completed bachelor’s and master’s programs at the Institute of Applied Sciences. University leaders encouraged the graduates to create their own employment opportunities rather than solely seeking them.

Dr. Olivier Habimana, Director in charge of Technology and Research at the Higher Education Council, told graduates that innovation and entrepreneurship are essential for meeting Rwanda's employment goals. rw.headline: Rwanda farmers urged to innovate against climate change

paragraphs: Rwanda's farmers must adopt innovative agricultural methods to counter threats to food and livestock production from changing weather patterns. Agriculture and Animal Resources Minister Dr Telesphore Ndabamenye made this call on Friday, October 30, during World Food Day celebrations in Gatsibo District.

Minister Ndabamenye urged farmers to increase productivity for household consumption and market supply, identifying climate change as a major challenge. He advised adopting farming techniques that reduce reliance on rainfall and prepare for disasters.

Farmers were also encouraged to follow best practices like timely planting, correct fertiliser application, and proper harvesting and storage to minimize losses. Livestock farmers should ensure sufficient animal feed and consider crop and livestock insurance.

rw.headline: Kagame tells officials to assess performance
rw.dek: President Paul Kagame urged public officials to regularly assess their performance and improve public service.
paragraphs: President Paul Kagame urged public officials to regularly assess their performance and improve how they serve citizens, stating that their decisions impact ordinary people. Kagame spoke on Friday, October 30, during the swearing-in of four senior officials at Village Urugwiro in Kigali.

The newly sworn-in officials include Julienne Uwacu as Minister of Public Service and Labour, Judith Uwizeye moving to the Senate, Claudette Mukashyaka as Auditor General of State Finances, and Gratien Kubwimana as Deputy Auditor General. Kagame stated that changes in responsibilities should prompt leaders to examine past performance and identify areas for improvement.

The president emphasized that this self-reflection should extend to all individuals with government responsibilities, regardless of whether they are taking on new roles or continuing existing ones. He stressed that public service should be evaluated by its impact on others, not solely by the positions held.

st.headline: Sao Tome and Principe and Mozambique sign air service deal
st.dek: The agreement aims to establish future air links between the two Lusophone nations to boost bilateral cooperation.
paragraphs: Sao Tome and Principe and Mozambique signed an air service agreement in Maputo on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The deal is intended to create conditions for future air connections between the two countries, strengthening bilateral cooperation and integrating African civil aviation. António Lima, president of Sao Tome and Principe's National Institute of Civil Aviation (INAC), and Emanuel da Conceição Chaves, president of Mozambique's Institute of Civil Aviation (IACM), signed the document.

The signing took place during a seminar on Civil Aviation Development in Lusophone Countries. Irina Ribeiro, permanent secretary of Mozambique's Ministry of Transport and Communications, was present. This agreement aligns with efforts to promote air connectivity among African nations, supporting the African Union's Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM) initiative.

SAATM seeks to liberalize air transport across the continent and ease the movement of people and goods. Mozambique's national airline is Linhas Aéreas de Moçambique (LAM), which flies to various countries, while Sao Tome and Principe has STP Airways, offering weekly flights to Lisbon.

sn.headline: Faye calls for lasting legacy from Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics
sn.dek: Senegal's president urged investment in sport as a tool for economic and social development.
paragraphs: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye advocated on Saturday, October 31, 2026, for lasting investment in sport to drive economic and social development in Africa. Speaking at the Summit on Sport and Sustainable Development in Dakar, ahead of the Youth Olympic Games (Joj) opening ceremony, Faye stressed the need to leverage the international competition's legacy. He stated that the Dakar Joj should foster a strong sporting youth and a sports economy for development.

Faye, addressing heads of state and international delegates, including the IOC president, highlighted the Joj as an opportunity to convert Africa's sporting potential into economic and social gains. He emphasized a sports policy encompassing school and university sport, amateur practice, high-level competition, training, coaching, and infrastructure financing. The president noted that these conditions would encourage talent, attract investment, and create a sports economy.

The Senegalese leader pointed to investments made for Dakar 2026, including new and renovated sports facilities, which he believes will provide spaces for youth and communities, strengthen social cohesion, and foster citizen engagement. Faye assured that the state would mobilize national resources to preserve this legacy and monitor summit conclusions. He also condemned racism in sport and called for peace and cooperation.

sn.dek: The feast honours all saints in the Christian faith, reminding believers of their call to holiness.
paragraphs: Senegalese Christians observed All Saints' Day on Sunday, November 1, commemorating all the saints of the Church. The occasion involved prayers to honour men and women who demonstrated their faith in Jesus Christ during their earthly lives.

Abbé Joseph Tendeng, vicar at the Notre-Dame des Pauvres parish in Tilène, clarified that the feast is not for the dead but for all saints. He urged believers to understand the true meaning of this significant Christian celebration.

The day serves as a moment for reflection and a reminder of each Christian's vocation to holiness. It encourages followers to live out their faith through actions and love for their neighbours, striving for a more just world.
